whole example (10/10; round 2: 8, 9, 6). Seed 1 misses only
the hard range: the generator drew one 643 B login of 192.168.1.21 on day 2, before the route
node of `/login` existed, and no node ever saw it (the first rows of a route are lost, 16.11.8
item 2); on seed 0, where no login below 1 KB was generated at all, the learned range
[1 053, 2 616] B is the data's own range and passes (V4). Seed 3 misses two: the address-level
综合部 node states D1's window plus A2's 09:10–09:14 (IoU 0.69, threshold 0.7) and a band whose
fitted upper edge is 2.85 KB from 41 logins (truth 2 KB). Seeds 2 and 4 failed 6 and 2 clauses
in the first final runs (before V10): on seed 2 the login node had split on {grp:∅} on day 3.4
and later on the learned-group level, which put the one-address approver group of 192.168.1.21
into the `other` branch with 销售部; on seed 4 the ∅ split left no address-level 综合部 node by
day 21. Without the transient split the login node first splits 研发's pool /24s from the rest
(day 3.4–5.4) and then the departments' /24s (from day 8.4), and on both seeds the most specific
login statement for 综合部 names exactly its three addresses with their bindings (seed 4: first
seen on day 9, the user names closed on {jack, mike, mike.w, rose}).

Reading (against the requirement's example): the 综合部 login node names the three addresses,
their bindings (192.168.1.21 still `jack` on day 21 although A2 borrowed `rose` from it on days
17–21), the closed user-name set {jack, mike, mike.w, rose} with grammar `[a-z]{4}(\.[a-z])?`,
the band 1–2 KB and the data's range 1–2.6 KB; its window 08:32–08:51 is D1's new window (A2's
09:10 logins are no longer a window, R4). Its stated confidence 0.31 is the node's held-out hold
rate after the D1/D2 drifts. The department's view composes its two learned roles (the approver
192.168.1.21 and the report writers .23 / .121), and says that 综合部 never writes in finance —
"192.168.1.23 的尝试被判定为越权（未学习）": A1's write was judged foreign and not learned,
which is the requirement's "访问财务系统去审批就是异常". The role group of the approver also says
what it never does inside OA ("在 oa 中从未执行：提交报告", deviation G13). The OA approval statements are
`stale` on day 21: D3 renamed the routes on day 14; P10 adopted the rename on day 17 (R3), but the
`/flow/` nodes are still candidates (16.11.8 item 4). Finance's approval is "财务部（192.168.2.10）"
only, in its two workday windows 10:00–11:28 and 15:01–15:58.


#### 16.11.7 Variants, non-regression and resources

- **O-red seed 0** (41 min, peak RSS 1.53 GB): recall by day d5 0.28, d7 0.35, d8 0.39, d10 0.58, d14 0.59, d21 0.68; precision by day d7 0.43, d8 0.53, d14 0.52, d21 0.75; ECE@14 0.29; false splits per system-month 0.0; anomalies 8/10 (missed: A4, A7); GA login who = the truth IPs True, finance approver only True, ARI 0.89, portal bindings 50; FAR >= LOW / >= MEDIUM 0.0056 / 0.0043
- **O60 seed 0** (21 min, peak RSS 1.09 GB): recall by day d5 0.32, d7 0.47, d8 0.50; precision by day d7 0.56, d8 0.67

- **O60 (aggregated vs 60-s event mode, PG1 at day 8 within 0.05):** days 1–7 are the same
  aggregated stream as pack O (day 7 recall 0.47 against pack O's 0.42, seed 0); on day 8, in
  60-s event mode, recall 0.50 against pack O's 0.48 on its aggregated day 8 (difference 0.02,
  inside 0.05; round 2: 0.053), precision 0.67 against 0.56. Its ten anomalies fall after day 8.
- **O-red** (never tuned on): recall@14 0.59 (round 2: 0.41), 8 of 10 anomalies (round 2: 7;
  missed now A4 and A7, round 2 A2, A3, A4), no false splits.
- **O-real (PG11)** was run once this round by the truth / cost / scale owner on a code snapshot
  of 04:49Z (before the final code): 3 of 12 R items pass (R8, R10, R11), 4 of 10 anomalies over
  35 days, recall / precision @14 0.45 / 0.17 (`reports/progressive/round3_eval/O-real_0.json`).
  It was not re-run on the final code (35 days ≈ 85 min of wall time).
- **PG4** points are the 7-day points of `reports/progressive/round3_eval/scale7` (20 000 IPs,
  340 attributes, 20 / 100 / 300 systems; code snapshot of 04:49Z, timings taken with 3–4 heavy
  processes on 4 cores): memory slope vs IPs 0.040, CPU/event slope vs IPs −0.157, memory slope
  vs attributes 0.172, CPU/event slope vs attributes 0.149 (round 2: 0.236, fail → pass), idle
  system 0.45 MB, largest tree 14.2 MB pass; memory slope vs systems 0.45 (> 0.3) and the per-event
  p95 (scoring 6.4 ms, learning 5.6 ms against 100 / 250 µs; the maximum over all points,
  dominated by the servers packs' 5–30 k events) fail. The engines changed after the snapshot
  (V2–V6, V10) add no per-event work.
- **PG9 / non-regression:** packs A and E seed 0 with the default registry are identical to
  round 4, key for key apart from timings (0 differences each). They were run before V10, which
  changes P04 only; the default registry (`full`) does not run the P-core, so V10 cannot change
  them (the round's other P04 changes did not either).
- **Per run:** 39–41 min wall (seeds 0–4; O-red 41 min, O60 21 min) with 3–4 heavy processes on
  4 cores, peak RSS 1.45–1.94 GB (round 2: 1.26–1.30 GB). The peak includes the checkpoint
  serialisation of the resumable runner (a 300–420 MB pickle of the whole run state every ~10
  minutes); the engines' own state was not measured separately. Engine CPU per run 2 020–2 110 s
  (round 2: 1 760 s at lower machine load; P04 280–291 s against 253 s, P03 91–100 s against
  72 s).
- **Runs repeated after V10:** the first final runs (code before V10) are kept in
  `reports/progressive/round3_eval/pre_v10_runs/`. With V10, seeds 0 and 1 and O-red score
  identically (the transient splits there were candidates or absent), seed 2 gains 1 truth pattern
  at day 14 and 6 checklist clauses, seed 4 halves its FAR ≥ MEDIUM (0.0067 → 0.0037) and gains
  2 clauses, seed 3 loses 1 truth pattern at day 14 (销售部's closed set at a node the new tree
  builds later) and 1 clause (window IoU 0.72 → 0.69).


#### 16.11.8 Diagnosis of what still fails (by engine)

Per truth pattern at day 14, the misses of the 5 seeds (190 eligible rows, 42 missed; driver
`prog3/evl/diag.py`, scratch logs `diagZ_s*.txt`):

and views; evaluation, cost and scale), then the evaluator measured one final code state. 16.12.1 – 16.12.6 are
the evaluation owner's part (gate semantics, determinism, cost, O-real and O-servers); 16.12.7 – 16.12.9 the
method of the final runs, the evaluator's changes EV-1 – EV-11 and a summary of the owners' engine changes
T-1 – T-7, C-1 – C-6, G-1 – G-6; 16.12.10 – 16.12.16 the results, the example verbatim, the diagnosis and the
open issues. The Chinese narrative is the design doc §3.0, §3.3 and §3.8.0 – §3.8.0c.

`scripts/progressive_report.py`, P12 `system_profile.py`, P15 `resource_governor.py`, new

#### 16.12.2 How much of ECE@14 = 0.23 is semantics

Round-3 runs (`reports/progressive/runs`, 5 seeds), per-statement records replicated from
`pg1_snapshot` (same held-out draws; day-14 ECE identical to the published one on every seed):

| Seed | ECE@14 (n) | null floor @14 | pooled days ≥ 7: n / plug-in ECE / null floor / debiased CE | stated / held | nodes stated / held | parts stated / held |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.231 (62) | 0.121 | 841 / 0.268 / 0.034 / 0.320 | 0.48 / 0.73 | 0.49 / 0.69 | 0.46 / 0.80 |
| 1 | 0.220 (67) | – | 894 / 0.200 / 0.032 / 0.244 | 0.55 / 0.74 | 0.54 / 0.69 | 0.57 / 0.83 |
| 2 | 0.233 (74) | – | 981 / 0.291 / 0.030 / 0.327 | 0.48 / 0.76 | 0.47 / 0.72 | 0.48 / 0.85 |
| 3 | 0.246 (63) | – | 842 / 0.259 / 0.036 / 0.334 | 0.51 / 0.76 | 0.51 / 0.72 | 0.51 / 0.83 |
| 4 | 0.265 (60) | – | 810 / 0.228 / 0.036 / 0.279 | 0.56 / 0.76 | 0.56 / 0.74 | 0.55 / 0.79 |

Reading: almost none of it. With n ≈ 60 a perfectly calibrated set would show 0.12, but the
floor does not add to a real bias (the expected plug-in ECE of a set biased by δ ≈ 0.2 is ≈ δ);
pooled over days 7–21 (floor 0.03) the plug-in ECE is 0.20–0.29 and the debiased error 0.24–0.33.
Duplicated claims: 0. Statements with no held-out event of their context (counted false; e.g.
D3's renamed approval pages on day 14): 3 on day 14 of seed 0, pooled ECE 0.268 → 0.273 without
them. What remains is genuine under-confidence: statements stated 0.48–0.56 and held 0.73–0.77,
parts (stated like their node, held by their own members) more than nodes. The round-4 engines
reduce it (below) but the pooled error is still 0.15–0.23 there: the gate remains failed for a
reason the engines own (P04 `p_hold`, P14 part confidence).

- P07 / P02 (content, tree): value sketches whose retained values depend on set-iteration
  order (`pgrammar` finance `body.kv.lines[]` optional values, `pregistry` hier `set_keep`) —
  identical runs differ across processes unless `PYTHONHASHSEED` is pinned; P11 cover lists
  unsorted; P08 bound shares summed in set order.
- P12 (this owner, not fixed): O-real R13's twelve CRM branch servers never form their family —
  they expose two route prefixes (`/crm/customer/*`, `/crm/visit`) and `pfamily.informative`
  asks for three, although their pairwise Jaccard is 0.82–0.99 (`prog4/eval/r13_diag_before.jsonl`).
  Admitting a named service with ≥ 1 route prefix was tried and REVERTED: the branches then
  joined pack O's own `crm` (same host, same routes, different users) in one family; the merged
  tree was 69 × a single CRM tree and the CRM systems' recall fell to 0 (overall O-real
  recall@14 0.49 → 0.12; `prog4/eval/final/oreal4_e410/`). A family rule also has to respect
  disjoint user populations (or the scorer has to map a family's statements back to all its
  systems) before small applications can be admitted.
- P04 / P14 (tree, views): calibration — under-confidence remains the whole of PG2's
  calibration error (16.12.2), largest for group parts and for days 7–10.
- Lead: the calibration target 0.05 now reads a pooled debiased error; at ~800 judged claims
  per run its sampling standard deviation is 0.015–0.02 (simulation: a calibrated set reads
  0.011, 95 % of runs below 0.038; a bias of 0.05 reads 0.046, of 0.15 reads 0.141).

#### 16.12.7 Round 4 on the final code: what was measured

Everything below is measured on ONE code state: HEAD 303dac6 plus the four owners' uncommitted
round-4 work (tree / calibration P04 · `pnode` · `ptree`; content / time P06 – P10; conformity /
groups / views P03 · P11 · P14; evaluation / cost P12 · P15 · `pmetrics` · `pscale` · `orggen`) plus the
evaluator's changes EV-1 – EV-11 below. Runs: pack O seeds 0–4, 21 days at 900 s, registry
`progressive_decision`, `--no-series`, resumable (checkpoint every ~15 min of wall time), `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`;
O60 and O-real (35 days) seed 0; packs A and E seed 0 with the default registry. Pack O seeds 0–4 were run
last on the final tree (`code8`, EV-1 – EV-11); O60 and O-real on `code7` (EV-1 – EV-8: without EV-10 / EV-11,
which change only how P14 words the user view's action lists and a part's bindings) and O-red seed 0 on the
final candidate before EV-7 / EV-8 (`code6`): EV-7, EV-8, EV-10 and EV-11 change only what P14 renders
(EV-8's `p_hold` feeds nothing but P14), so their pipelines — tree, constraints, incidents — are the final
code's, while their statements carry the earlier views and confidences. Every pack O score of `code8` other
than the rendered text equals `code7`'s on seed 0, and on seeds 1–4 differs only where a part's changed
binding evidence re-draws the evaluator's sample (16.12.15 item 8). Seeds 0–1 were used for development and seed 2 to
confirm; the content owner also ran seed 3 (for the seed-3 checklist clauses) on an intermediate state, and
the evaluator's EV-4 – EV-8 were derived on seeds 0–2; seed 4 was not looked at before the final runs.

**A measurement defect found on the way: the code snapshots had no signatures.** The owners'
run snapshots (`git archive HEAD backend scripts`) and this round's first evaluator snapshots
lacked `data/`, which `build.py` reads the signature library from (`data/signatures`, relative
to the code), so `signature.rule_match` / `signature.correlation` ran with no rules in every
owner's pack O number of round 4. Round 3's final runs had `data/`. The final runs below have it;
the owners' figures quoted in their reports are therefore not exactly comparable with these.

**Before / after.** "Before" is round 3's final runs (`reports/progressive/round3/runs`, the
pickles of §16.11) re-scored by this round's scorer (§16.12.1 E4-4 – E4-7, EV-1): same
generator, same truth, same held-out law, so the comparison measures the engines only. The
round-3 figures as published in §16.11 are quoted where they matter.

IoU 0.69 → 0.86 through C-2 / C-3). The one miss is seed 3's 90 % band: fitted 956–2 859 B on n_eff = 25.6 and displayed
1–3 KB. The truth puts 90 % in 1–2 KB and a 5 % uniform tail in 2–3 KB, so the density drops sharply at the
true 95th percentile and an over-drawn tail moves the sample quantile into it; the content owner's simulation
found no quantile estimator that holds ±20 % at this n (86 % of draws at n = 41; Harrell–Davis worse), so the
estimator was not changed.

#### 16.12.15 Diagnosis of what still fails

1. **Precision 0.857 @14 (target 0.90) is mostly drift lag.** Seeds 0–4, day 14 (final `code8` runs): 48 of 335 judged claims fail
   (the evaluator's scratch scripts `precdecE.py` / `precdrift.py`, not in the repository, re-run by the docs owner on the final pickles): by failing constraint kind (a claim can fail several) `when` 19,
   no held-out event ("unsupported") 18 — 15 D3-renamed approval routes, 3 health-monitor group parts — `bind` 13, grammar 8, closed set 7, who 2; nodes 35, parts 13. Most are the three
   drifts of days 12–14: D1's login / home windows (still 08:49–09:21 on day 14 — day 13 is a Sunday, so one
   workday of the new window exists), D2's mike → mike.w (binding, grammar and closed set of the login node),
   D3's approval pages renamed on day 14 itself. On the actions no drift touched, day-14 precision is
   0.977 / 0.917 / 0.909 / 0.977 / 0.951 (seeds 0–4). Day 21: 34 of 352 fail — `when` 26 (16 nodes stating
   coverage 0.84–1.00 and holding 0.65–0.98, among them 4 `/flow/` statements carrying the old approval windows at
   0.95–0.96; 10 group parts stating 0.76–1.00 and holding 0.29–0.96, worst the sparse mail groups and finance
   parts), group parts of the health monitor with no held-out event 6, two bands (CRM `customer=` 0.87 / 0.81,
   portal comment size 0.86 / 0.66), grammar 2, closed set 1.
2. **Recall 0.842 @14.** Recurring misses: GA's 17:00 report submission (`GA.oa.report#1`: who, when and
   content all fail on day 14 on all 5 seeds; recovered by day 21 on 4 of 5), DEV's login
   (truth: a closed set of ~60 pool user names; the engine honestly states it open), the mail departments
   (GA / FIN / SALES mail differ only by short windows; who at /24 mixes departments), FIN's documents part
   (who), FIN's approval content on seeds 1–4 (on seed 1 the content owner traced it to the opinion set C-1
   leaves open: its rarest value seen ~1 in 20 arrivals), the 01:00 backup at day 21 (all 5 seeds).
3. **Calibration (pooled CE 0.157, target 0.05).** Nodes remain under-confident (stated 0.77, held 0.89, CE
   0.21); group parts are close (0.78 / 0.86, CE 0.11). The engine's internal tests still disagree with the
   evaluator's independent draws on transport bands and wide windows; on O-real the same machinery is
   over-confident (0.81 / 0.33). The debiased CE has a sampling sd of 0.015–0.02 at ~900 claims.
4. **PG5 D1 (seeds 3, 4) and D4 (seeds 3, 4).** D1 confirms the new window after 4 and 5 workdays (≤ 3
   required; seed 3's 综合部 node had only 2 dates before the change, too few for `regime_cut`); seed 4 also
   counts 2 incidents on the three addresses before confirmation, which are A2 / A4-type findings (credential,
   temporal) the D1 check does not separate from the drift. D4: one LOW single-tick incident of the same portal
   source 192.168.9.9 on both seeds (2025-09-16 20:45 UTC, `conf_seq` p = 2.4e-4; seed 3 reopened the next day by
   `conf_content` p = 7.2e-5). **Diagnosed (probes on seed 0, `prog4/ev5/probe/`): these are B24's randomised
   conformal p of a tie, not a P03 finding.** 192.168.9.9 is the AUTO health monitor (GET /health every 60 s on
   oa, finance and portal), scored in every tick; its conf_who / conf_seq score is 0 (pm = 1: nothing unusual)
   on almost every tick, so its B24 ring is all zeros (n = 256, no GPD tail) and a score of 0 receives
   `p = U` (the seeded tie-breaking uniform of `m_calib.uniform(system, entity, detector, ts)`, exactly
   uniform under the null by design). Seed 0, day 18, 02:00: oa conf_who p = 7.92e-5 with score 0 and pm = 1.0;
   finance 02:15 the same (6.1e-5). Because U is seeded by (system, entity, detector, ts) and the monitor's
   ticks are the same on every seed, the same incident (oa, 1758132000, conf_who 7.921e-05) opens on all five
   seeds, and the portal one of seeds 3 / 4 is the same draw. Probe 1 / 2 found no per-event P03 p below 1e-3 for
   the monitor at those ticks, and B29 has no violated constraint to show (it falls back to the request count).
   Across the final runs 4 – 7 of ~70 incidents per seed are conformity-only alarms without any P03 finding
   (`ev5/noev.py`; the monitor's included). This is the lib-3 decision chain's null budget spent on coin flips
   for detectors with an atom at pm = 1, well within the FAR gate (≥ LOW 0.0027 per entity-day against
   ≤ 0.10) but an alarm with no evidence. Not changed here: B24's exact-null randomisation also feeds its KS
   health weights and B25's meta rings, and packs A–E share it (open issue for the lib-3 decision owner).
5. **PG10.** Day 11: only seed 2 has a 综合部-only login statement before D1; on seed 1 the department's part
   of the shared login node states its own band (EV-5) 1–2.5 KB from 17 points (truth 1–2 KB, +25 % > 20 %);
   seeds 0, 3, 4 have no 综合部 login statement on day 11. Day 21: seed 3's band 1–3 KB; seed 4's window
   08:30–08:45 stated at 85 % (a 15-minute stretch of the uniform 08:30–08:51 law holds ~0.71).
6. **PG8 0.83** (finance's who arm `prefix` on seeds 1, 3, 4 against ip / grp) and who level within 5 % 2/5 —
   unchanged; the decisions are now reproducible (E4-1).
7. **PG4** per-event p95 (6.8 / 6.4 ms on the servers points); the cost profile is in 16.12.4.
8. **Views (fixed: EV-10, EV-11).** The department and group views' action lists kept the old route names after
   a P10-adopted rename, and group parts repeated the other members' bindings and `… 只来自 …` clauses. Both are
   rendering only: the final runs (`code8`) score identically to the runs without them on seed 0; on seeds 1 – 4
   a few part claims change their binding evidence, so the evaluator's per-claim draw changes (the claim key
   includes the bindings); each flipped claim has the same verdict under the old draws (`ev5/flip.py`).

Tried and reverted this round: falsifying young P09 windows from held-out tests (tree owner; seed 0 recall@14
0.82 → 0.68), freezing a statement's prior at its first test (T-4 first version; replaced by EV-8), held-out
tests of 100 units at 3 σ (EV-4 first version), P07 closure by daily tests (content owner; too slow on young
split nodes), forward-split window coverage (halved FIN mail's coverage; replaced by date-blocked CV), recency
weighting of non-full reservoirs, deleting (instead of folding) duplicate ancestor statements (seed 1 recall
−0.024 to −0.048), and admitting two-route named services as families (O-real recall@14 0.49 → 0.12).

#### 16.12.16 Open issues (round 4 → owners)

- **Tree / time (P04, P09):** drift lag at the day-14 snapshot (a change < 3 dates old is kept provisional by
  C-3, but the node statement keeps the old binding / grammar / closed set until D2's new value is confirmed);
  `when` coverage over-stated by 0.04–0.08 on wide or sparse windows; D1 confirmation on nodes with < 3 dates
  before the change; node under-confidence on pack O vs over-confidence on O-real (P04 `p_hold`).
- **Views (P14):** parts of health monitors stated with no held-out support; P11's sticky group label keeps the
  old page name (`综合部·oa GET /approval/list`) after a rename.
- **Lib-3 decision chain (B24 / B25):** a score at its atom (score 0, pm = 1) receives a randomised p = U on an
  all-tie ring, and B25's single-tick path can alarm on it: 4 – 7 of ~70 incidents per pack O seed are
  conformity-only alarms without any P03 finding, among them the health monitor's on every seed and PG5 D4's
  failures on seeds 3 / 4 (16.12.15 item 4). Candidate: keep the randomised p for calibration health and the
  meta rings but let the decision paths treat a tie at the atom as p = 1 (a coin flip is no evidence); needs the
  packs A–E non-regression.
- **Content (P07):** small-population closed sets whose rarest member is rare (FIN opinions) — open by design;
  whether the truth should demand DEV's 60-name closed set (lead).
- **Evaluation:** D1's incident count includes attack findings on the same addresses; PG2's "80 % by day 7"
  (day-7 recall 0.44–0.52) against the design's evidence requirements (lead); O-red was scored with `code6`'s
  views; one O-real seed only; PG9 on packs B–D and seeds 1–4 not run.
- **P12:** R13 (CRM branches never form a family; the two-route admission rule is unsafe), PG8's finance who arm.
- **Cost:** per-event p95 10–60× the target; hot spots in P04, P05, P02, P08 (16.12.4).
- **Hash order:** P07 / P02 value sketches and P11 cover lists depend on set iteration order (pinned
  `PYTHONHASHSEED` hides it; 16.12.6).

### 16.13 Round 5: results on the final code (2026-10-06)

Four owners worked at the same time on top of 180f1fc. The tree owner covered P04, P05 and their libraries. The registry, content and binding owner covered P00–P02 and P06–P08. The lib-3 decision-chain owner covered B24, B25, `calib` and `m_calib`. The time, groups and views owner covered P03, P09–P11, P14 and P15. The round had three themes: per-event cost, determinism, and the lower-atom tie rule. After the owners finished, the evaluator measured the final code (16.13.1).

- 16.13.1–16.13.3 cover the method, the owners' changes and the evaluator's changes (EV5-1 – EV5-7).
- 16.13.4–16.13.10 cover the results.
- 16.13.11–16.13.12 cover the diagnosis and the open issues.

The Chinese narrative is the design doc §3.0 (status per requirement sentence), §3.3 (the round-5 changes in place, numbered T5-*, R5-*, C5-*, V5-* there to keep them apart from round 4's T-* / C-*), §3.8.0–§3.8.0c (round 5; round 4 kept as §3.8.0d, round 3 as §3.8.0e, round 2 as §3.8.0f), §3.9.11–§3.9.12 (the lower-atom rule) and §3.11.

#### 16.13.1 What was measured

**Code state.** Two engine states were measured; every score uses the final scorer.
- **`code4`** is commit 49263f5 (the lead's round-5 checkpoint): HEAD 180f1fc plus three sets of changes.
  - The four owners' round-5 work (16.13.2).
  - The evaluator's EV5-1 to EV5-4 (16.13.3).
  - The snapshot's `data/` directory (the signature library). The defect of round 4's owner snapshots (§16.12.7) did not recur.
- **`code5`** is `code4` plus EV5-5 and EV5-6.
  - EV5-5 changes only an emission order.
  - EV5-6 changes only the view of a system that joined a family, and no pack O seed has one.

**Which runs used which state.**
- Pack O seeds 0–4 and the determinism run used `code4`.
- O-real 0–2, O-red, O60, packs A / E and the PG4 points used `code5`.

**The final scorer.** The final tree is `code5` plus EV5-7 (scorer only). Every O-real / O-red / O60 run, and round 4's pickles, were re-scored with it (`prog5/ev/rescore5.py`). Re-scoring pack O seed 0 with it changes nothing (0 of 15 735 leaves).

**Runs.**
- Pack O: seeds 0–4, 21 days at 900 s, registry `progressive_decision`, `--no-series`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`.
- Pack O seed 0 once more with `PYTHONHASHSEED=1` (determinism, 16.13.6).
- O-red and O60: seed 0.
- O-real (35 days): seeds 0–2.
- Packs A and E: seed 0 with the default registry (`scripts/evaluate.py`).
- The PG4 points: the `scripts/progressive_scale.py` grid, 7 days.

The pack runs use the resumable runner (`eval/resumable.run_pack_resumable`), which writes a checkpoint at a day end every ~15 min of wall time. The driver is the evaluator's scratch script `prog5/ev/drv5.py`: `run_pack_resumable` plus `progressive_report._score`, the same scorer as the report. At most two heavy processes ran at a time on the 4-core machine.

**Before and after.** "Before" means round 4's final runs (`reports/progressive/round4/runs`, the pickles of §16.12) re-scored by this round's scorer. EV5-1 to EV5-3 change what D4, gate 7 / `ks_conf` and PG4 read, so the re-score is needed for a fair comparison. Round 4's published numbers stay in `reports/progressive/round4/`, and the re-scored report is in `reports/progressive/round4/rescored_r5/`.

**HEAD did not reproduce round 4's runs.** The tree owner and the time / views owner ran HEAD in the same harness and got different results from `reports/progressive/runs/O_*.json`. For example, seed 2 had recall@14 0.816 against 0.842. The cause was state that depended on memory addresses, which `PYTHONHASHSEED` does not pin:
- P03's `HourSS` broke heap ties by `id(key)`.
- P04 kept the `id()` of its reference statement (`meta.hold_fp._ref`).

Both are fixed this round (V-5 and T-5 below), and the determinism check (16.13.6) now passes. The owners' before/after tables compare against HEAD runs from their own harness. This section compares against round 4's own runs, re-scored.

#### 16.13.6 Determinism

Pack O seed 0 was run twice on `code4`, once with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and once with `PYTHONHASHSEED=1`, in separate processes.

- **Scores.** The score JSONs are identical: 0 differences in 15 735 leaves (`jdiff.py`, timings excluded).
- **Full result pickle.** A deep diff (`pkldiff.py`; `reports/progressive/round5_eval/determinism_pkl_diff.txt`) found two differences, both order-only:
  - B27 emitted the same incident events of one tick (2025-09-21 01:15 UTC: one oa reopen and twelve portal opens) in a different order.
  - 196 `hold_facets` dicts of `model.ptree` had a different key order.
  - Everything else is equal: all events and incidents, every snapshot model, every statement, every value.
- **Fix.** EV5-5 sorts both.

In round 4 the same check needed `PYTHONHASHSEED` pinned, and even then two processes differed through `id()`-based state (16.13.1). Round 5 removed the str-hash dependences: T-4, R-4 and V-5 owner-side, and EV5-5. The owners' subprocess tests run under several hash seeds:
- `test_p04_p05_stream_equivalence.py` (P04 / P05 models);
- `test_registry_hash_order.py` (P02 / P06 / P07 / P08, under 5 hash seeds);
- `test_round5_hash_order_views.py` (P03 / P11 / P15, under 5 seeds);
- `test_round5_eval_order.py` (EV5-5).

`pscale.pin_hash_seed` still pins the evaluation entry points to 0, which keeps the old reports reproducible.

*Memory against round 4's report.* The memory points are 5–30 % above round 4's report, but they equal HEAD's on the same pack: servers-20 is 42.4 MB on HEAD and 42.2 MB on `code5`. The difference is the pack / code state behind round 4's older points, not round 5.

*Learning p95.* It reads 2.3 ms against 6.4 ms in round 4. Most of that is EV5-3's denominator: P04's own learned rows rather than P00's rows of the same tick.

#### 16.13.8 PG9: bounded vs full (calibration owner's runs, round-5 lib-3 code)

These runs (`reports/progressive/round5_eval/pg9/`) use the lib-3 decision chain owner's final code. They come before the other owners' last edits, EV5-2 (gate 7 reads D⁺) and EV5-5 / EV5-6. Those edits do not touch the default registry's bounded mode, except gate 7's reading. The machine was shared with 2–5 heavy processes.

**Bounded-mode failures shared with HEAD (open issues, 16.13.12):**
- Gate 15. Pack A has 88 stale series (B11 `behavior.timing` 38, `behavior.acc_alarm` 28) from the B11 / B13 prefilter, and 68 `pipeline_degraded` events, because B13 writes `insufficient_support:budget_history` for the IPs it skips. Pack E has 58 stale series.
- Gate 8. On A, T9b `unknown_identity` is lost and the EER share falls 1.0 → 0.67. On E, 19 of 37 keys have no identity / portrait profile.
- Pack A clean CUSUM edges rise 10 → 24 in bounded mode. 19 of them are hourly S_h alarms of erp-prod|10.20.4.32, from `robust_tail` trimming a small ring.

PG9 stays "not measured" in the gate table. The assembly has no packs A–E on/off comparison input (`pg9_compare`), as in round 4.

**O-real (35 days; seeds 0–2 on `code5`).** Each run took 4 365 / 4 398 / 4 423 s of wall time in one resumable process (4–5 checkpoints), with peak RSS ≈ 3.2 GB and 0 exceptions. Every O-real number below uses the round-5 scorer with EV5-7. "Round 4" is round 4's seed-0 pickle re-scored the same way. Its published 0.304 / 0.406 @35 and CE 0.522 had judged every family statement "unsupported".

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| recall / precision @14 | 0.446 / 0.438 | 0.569 / 0.570 | 0.462 / 0.450 | 0.477 / 0.421 | 0.492 / 0.421 |
| recall / precision @35 | 0.342 / 0.754 | 0.392 / 0.770 | 0.354 / 0.747 | 0.405 / 0.747 | 0.342 / 0.824 |
| anomalies | 4/10 (A1, A8, A9, A10) | same | same | same | same |
| FAR ≥ LOW / ≥ MEDIUM | 0.0033 / 0.0024 | 0.0017 / 0.0012 | 0.0017 / 0.0012 | 0.0037 / 0.0024 | 0.0021 / 0.0014 |

**Reading.**
- **Calibration.** Round 4 read O-real's statements as strongly over-confident: stated 0.81, held 0.33. Most of that was the scorer, not the engine. oa and its replica oa-r2 form the engine family `fam:1` from day 11; the truth calls that family `oa`, so none of `fam:1`'s statements was judged against their events (EV5-7). With the family judged, O-real is over-confident by 0.15–0.21 (CE 0.20–0.27), where pack O is under-confident by 0.08.
- **What EV5-6 costs on seed 0.** It costs recall and precision @14: 0.569 / 0.570 → 0.462 / 0.450. Before the fix, oa's frozen pre-join view still held its unchanged patterns, and on day 14 the 3-day-old family tree had not restated all of them. EV5-6 is what lets D3 pass on O-real; D3 also passes on seeds 1–2.
- **Recall over the run.** O-real's recall falls from day 14 to day 35 on every run, as in round 4.
- **R13 and the example.** R13 (CRM branches as one family) fails on all seeds, as in round 4. The example checklist reads the family view (EV5-7) and passes 3–4 of 10.

**O-red (seed 0, `code5`).**
- Recall / precision @14 0.622 / 0.780; round 4 re-scored: 0.568 / 0.776.
- Recall / precision @21 0.773 / 0.919; round 4: 0.705 / 0.926.
- Anomalies 9/10 (A7 missed, as in round 4). False splits 0. FAR ≥ LOW / ≥ MEDIUM 0.0027 / 0.0020 (0.0029 / 0.0020). D1–D5 all pass.
- Pooled CE 0.163, stated 0.78 / held 0.86 (round 4: 0.207, 0.73 / 0.85).

**O60 (seed 0, `code5`).** O60 aggregates days 1–7 and switches to 60-s events from day 8. Its day-8 recall / precision is 0.559 / 0.774, against pack O seed 0's 0.545 / 0.839. Recall agrees within the 0.05 consistency requirement. Precision is 0.065 lower on 31 vs 31 judged claims (round 4: 0.500 / 0.829 against 0.545 / 0.838).

**Non-regression, default registry (packs A and E seed 0, `code5`, `scripts/evaluate.py`; `prog5/ev/ae5_keep`).**
- Compared with `reports/round4/runs/{A,E}_0_full.json`, the deltas are exactly the tie fix (C-1–C-3) plus gate 7 reading D⁺ (EV5-2). The score fields equal the calibration owner's final runs (`round5_eval/pg9/final_{A,E}_full.json`) apart from the KS reading.
- **Pack A:** detection 12/12, 8 within deadline, same severities. Incidents ≥ LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH 19 / 6 / 2 (same); reopened 5 → 9. Legit L8 low → medium. Classes ARI 0.780, EER share 1.0 (same).
- **Pack E:** 3/3 (T5' high → critical). LOW false alarms 8 → 6, MEDIUM 1 → 1. Classes ARI 0.755 → 0.551 and refit ARI min 0.955 → 0.689: B02 refit fragility through the governor trajectory, an open issue for B02.
- **Gate 7.** The anti-conservative D⁺ maximum is 0.102 on A (marg_int) and 0.128 on E (marg_shape_q). The two-sided D is 1.0 on both, the atom at p = 1 of `silence` and the other atom detectors.
- **Wall time.** A took 911 s against 1 048 s in round 4; E took 1 121 s against 1 283 s.

**Tests.** The final tree passes the full suite: 3 165 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed in 21 min (`prog5/ev/full2.txt`; round 4: 3 052). Before EV5-4b/c, EV5-5–EV5-7 it gave 3 153 passed. The evaluator's new tests:

- `tests/engines/test_round5_eval_order.py` (EV5-5)
- `tests/engines/test_p14_round5_eval.py` (EV5-6)
- `tests/eval/test_pmetrics.py::{test_d4_counts_only_incidents_that_involve_the_grown_population, test_engine_family_statements_are_judged_for_their_member_systems}`
- `tests/eval/test_metrics.py::test_calibration_gate_reads_the_anti_conservative_side`
- `tests/eval/test_pscale.py::test_learning_p95_divides_p04_cpu_by_the_rows_p04_learned`
- `tests/eval/test_progressive_report_label.py::test_example_reads_the_family_view_of_a_system_that_joined_one`

Each one fails on the code before its change. The owners' tests are listed in 16.13.2.

#### 16.13.11 Diagnosis of what still fails

1. **Precision @14: 0.842 (target 0.90). Most of the shortfall is drift that no engine could yet see.**
   - **The day-14 snapshot.** Day 14 is the Sunday after three drifts:
     - D1, Friday 12: one workday of the new login window.
     - D2, Saturday 13: `mike.w` has no event before Monday 15.
     - D3, Sunday 14: the renamed approval pages have no event before Monday 15.
   - **Why these claims fail.** The headline scorer judges every claim against the law valid that day. So two kinds of claims fail although no engine could have seen the change:
     - the old approval pages, which have no held-out event ("unsupported");
     - the login node's binding, grammar and closed set (`mike` → `mike.w`).
   - **Precision without them.** `precobs.py` (scratch) sets aside the claims on a lineage whose version valid that day has had no event yet: D2's login version and D3's three pages, matched by who-overlap with the changed version. On the remaining claims, precision@14 is 0.922 / 0.926 / 0.903 / 0.980 / 0.939 on seeds 0–4 (median 0.926). On round 4's runs it is 0.945 (median).
   - **What is left.** D1's login / home windows: one new workday, and a rank test cannot reach α = 0.01 on 3 arrivals (the time / views owner measured this; a location test false-flags day 11). Plus 'when' coverage on small samples.
   - The headline gate is NOT changed by the evaluator. Whether drift-touched claims should be judged only after a workday of the new behaviour is the lead's decision (open issue).
   - Precision@14 fell 0.857 → 0.842 against round 4. Part of the fall is V-1: it removed root `GET /health` statements that the evaluator had been passing (3 on seed 0, 2 on seed 1, per the time / views owner).
2. **Calibration: pooled debiased CE 0.129 [0.100–0.144] (target 0.05).**
   - It is better than round 4's 0.157 [0.149–0.192] on the same scorer.
   - Statements are still under-confident: pooled stated 0.807 against held 0.884 (round 4: 0.777 / 0.874).
   - The plug-in pooled ECE is 0.077 against a null floor of 0.026.
   - The remaining error is the same open issue as round 4: P04 `p_hold` for nodes and the P14 part confidence. On O-real the same machinery is over-confident (16.13.9).
3. **D1 on seeds 3 and 4: confirmed after 4 and 5 workdays (≤ 3 required).**
   - **The tree is in time.** On seed 3 the GA login node is confirmed with a new-regime window on workday 3 (day 16).
   - **P09's window fit is not.** It fits the window from the first three new-regime dates: 3 sources × 3 dates = 9 points, with back-off to the ancestor and coverage 0.8. The result is 08:38–08:51 against the true 08:30–08:51 (IoU 0.62 < 0.7). Seed 4 gives 08:31–08:44 (IoU 0.62). IoU passes on day 17 (seed 3) and day 18 (seed 4).
   - **The suggested fix does not settle it.** The tree owner suggested widening a few-point fit by range / (n − 1), the unbiased end-point correction for a uniform law. Applied to these fits:
     - Seed 3 becomes 08:36.4–08:52.6, IoU 0.65 — still below 0.7.
     - Seed 4 becomes 08:29.4–08:45.6, IoU 0.72.
   - The miss on seed 3 is sampling: 8 of 21 minutes are uncovered on the left edge, against an expected 2.1 for 9 uniform points. So the correction does not fix the gate, and it would widen every young window. Not changed; open issue for P09.
4. **AUTO.monitor.finance (seeds 1 and 4 at day 21; seed 2 at day 14).**
   - **What EV5-4 a–c fixed.** Three defects: the pooled reference level, the cross-type fallback, and a transient alarm kept open until expiry.
   - **What remains.** A weekend coded loss that rises between weekends. Seed 2: Saturday 13 reads 2.99 bits against the previous weekend's level of 2.35.
   - **Why.** P04's coder is shared by both day types and decays towards the workday mix between weekends. So the first weekend day reads as a change of the node.
   - It needs a day-type-conditioned coder, or a reference recomputed under the current coder (open issue, tree owner).
5. **Recurring misses (recall@14 0.842, @21 0.872).**
   - **On every seed:**
     - DEV's login: the truth demands the 60-name closed set of the pool, which the engine leaves open.
     - The 01:00 backup: one event a day, in the truth from day 21 only.
     - GA's 17:00 report submission at day 14 (`GA.oa.report#1`).
   - **On most seeds:**
     - The mail departments: GA / FIN / SALES mail differ only by short windows.
     - FIN's approval content at day 14: its opinion set is left open.
     - `PUB.portal.visit#3` at day 21 (seeds 0, 2, 4; content or when).
   - Recovered this round: `FIN.oa.documents#2` (V-4) on every seed.
6. **PG4.** Per-event p95 is still far above budget: scoring 6.9 ms and learning 2.3 ms against 100 / 250 µs, on the servers points dominated by per-tick overhead. The CPU per event rises faster with the number of attributes than allowed: 0.216 (0.238 in a load-paired re-run) against ≤ 0.2. P05 (×2.6 from 40 to 340 attributes), P02 (×1.9) and P00 (×3) carry that growth (16.13.7). The memory slopes pass.
7. **PG8 and PG10.** As in round 4:
   - PG8: finance's who arm, and who level within 5 % on 2/5 seeds. The time / views owner traced seed 1: the 3-consecutive-day switch rule, against the noise of the daily difference, delays the switch to day 18.
   - PG10: day 11 1/5 and day 21 3/5. On day 11 there is no 综合部-only login statement on seeds 0, 3 and 4. On day 21, seed 3's band is 1–3 KB and seed 4's window 08:30–08:45.
8. **PG11 (O-real).** 3–4 of 11 R-items per seed, as in round 4: R2–R5, R12 and R13 fail on all 3 seeds. With the family view judged (EV5-7), O-real's statements are over-confident by 0.15–0.21 (16.13.9).

Seeding a family tree from its members' confirmed nodes, or keeping a member's tree until the family has restated them, is untested.
- **Lib-3 decision chain (B24, B25):**
  - `robust_tail` can trim a small ring's own null extremes. In bounded pack A, erp-prod|10.20.4.32 gave q = 4e-5 for a score below its ring maximum and 19 hourly S_h alarm edges. Candidate: no trim below n_u ≈ 30. Needs the packs A–E non-regression.

It comes from P05 (×2.6 from 40 to 340 attributes), P02 (×1.9) and P00 (×3). Equivalent rewrites gave −8 % to −58 % per engine; the next steps need non-equivalent cadence changes:
  - spread P02's hourly `update_types` / `update_stats` over ticks;

  - P05's skip of unchanged keys with a decay-aware fingerprint (T-3);
  - P00's column-wise parser.
- **Ownership (lead):** `lib/pevalue.py` was in the time / views owner's brief but edited by the tree owner (its numba path).
- **numba (lead):** `numba` 0.68.0 and `llvmlite` 0.50.0 are installed in `.venv`, and `backend/requirements.txt` lists `numba>=0.60` as optional. Without it, or with `APPMON_NO_NUMBA=1`, the bit-identical numpy path runs. The JIT cache goes to `lib/__pycache__` (first compile 3–6 s).

### 16.14 Round 6: results on the final code (2026-10-12)

Four owners worked at the same time on top of ceb219c. The tree / family owner covered P04, P05, P12's family tree and their libraries. The temporal / workflow / views owner covered P03 (sequence side), P06–P11 and P14. The B-library owner covered B02, B11–B13, B18, B24 and the bounded-mode wiring. The scoring-cost owner covered P03's cost, `pscore`, `phier`, P02's hourly pass, P00's proxy resolution and the PG4 harness. The evaluator then measured the final code (16.14.1).

- 16.14.1–16.14.3 cover the method, the owners' changes and the evaluator's changes (EV6-1 – EV6-9).
- 16.14.4–16.14.10 cover the results.
- 16.14.11–16.14.12 cover the diagnosis and the open issues.
- The Chinese narrative (with the verbatim example in both views, including O-real day 35) is the design doc §3.0, §3.3 (the T6-* / V6-n / B6-* / S6-* numbering of the owners' changes) and §3.8.0 – §3.8.0c.

#### 16.14.1 What was measured

**Code state.** Every P-core run below used **`code11`**: commit d157721 (the lead's checkpoint with the four owners' work and the evaluator's EV6-1 – EV6-9); `code11` is identical to the final working tree (`backend/`, `scripts/`). Packs A and E (default registry, lib-3 only) do not run P05 and were measured on 7b9fa2e. Earlier evaluator snapshots, kept for comparison only:
- `code6` = 39cec3c: pack O seed 0.
- `code7` = `code6` + EV6-5b: pack O seeds 0–2, O-real seed 0.
- `code8` = 7b9fa2e: the full set of runs (`prog6/eval/f8`, `scale8`). `code7` and `code8` give identical pack O score JSONs on seeds 0 and 1.
- `code10` = `code8` + EV6-7 + the first version of EV6-8 (content-only memo key; `prog6/eval/f10`, `scale10`). Its memo shared one record version across registries (16.14.3); `code11` replaced it, and every result below was re-run.

**What EV6-7 / EV6-8 changed against `code8`** (same seeds, same scorer). Pack O: 23 / 360 / 304 / 1 555 / 55 of 16–19 k score leaves differ on seeds 0–4; recall @14 identical on every seed, seed 2 recall @21 0.857 → 0.881 and precision @14 0.969 → 0.953, the other headline figures within ±0.02; D1–D5, anomalies and checklists unchanged on every seed. (`code10` had differed from `code8` in 238 leaves on seed 0 alone: most of its deltas were the cross-registry collisions.) O-real: recall @14 0 to −0.03, @35 −0.03 to 0, FAR ≥ MEDIUM −0.0002 to 0, CE −0.015 to −0.008, anomalies and checklists unchanged. O-red: worse (16.14.9). PG4: 16.14.7.

**Runs.**
- Pack O: seeds 0–4, 21 days at 900 s, registry `progressive_decision`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, resumable runner (`eval/resumable.run_pack_resumable`, a checkpoint at a day end about every 15 min of wall time), scored by `progressive_report._score`, the report's own scorer (driver: the evaluator's scratch `prog6/eval/drv6.py`).
- Pack O seed 0 once more with `PYTHONHASHSEED=1` (determinism, 16.14.6).
- O-red and O60: seed 0. O-real (35 days): seeds 0–2.
- Packs A and E: seed 0 with the default registry (`scripts/evaluate.py`), full mode, and seed 0 in bounded mode (gate 15).
- PG4: the round-5 grid (IPs 500 / 20 000, attributes 340, servers 20 / 100 / 300), 7 days, resumable (`pscale.run_point_resumable`), thread CPU per engine (EV6-3) (`reports/progressive/scale_r6/`).

At most two heavy processes ran at a time on the 4-core machine. Unchanged lib-3 engines (B24–B28) ran about 1.4× slower than in round 5's runs, so wall-time comparisons between the rounds carry that factor; PG4 reads thread CPU (EV6-3).

**Before and after.** "Before" means round 5's final runs (`reports/progressive/round5/runs`, the pickles of §16.13) re-scored by this round's scorer (`reports/progressive/round5/rescored_r6/`). EV6-1 and EV6-2 change what precision and calibration judge, so the re-score is needed for a fair comparison. Round 5's published numbers stay in `reports/progressive/round5/`.

#### 16.14.6 Determinism

Pack O seed 0 was run twice on the final code in separate processes, with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` (`runs/O_0.json`) and `PYTHONHASHSEED=1` (`prog6/eval/f11h1/`).
- **Scores.** Identical: 0 differences in 16 612 leaves (`jdiff.py`, timings excluded).
- **Full result pickle.** The deep diff (`pkldiff.py`) found **0 differences**: every event, incident, snapshot model, statement and value is equal, including the orders that EV5-5 sorted in round 5.
- **Resumed = straight (EV6-8).** P05's generalisation memo was module-level and keyed on model sizes, so a run's results depended on what the process had memoised before; `test_resumable.py::test_resumed_run_equals_run_pack` failed in full-suite order. With the content fingerprint the full suite passes it (16.14.9).
- The owners' subprocess hash-seed tests pass (`test_p04_p05_stream_equivalence.py`, `test_registry_hash_order.py`, `test_round5_hash_order_views.py`, `test_round5_eval_order.py`), and the cost owner's P03 output digests matched the base code under `PYTHONHASHSEED` 0 and 1 (16.14.2).

- P09 costs about 50 % more than round 5 at equal load: round 6's session-weighted window fit (`_sessions`), the young-regime edges (`_young_edges`, which refits the previous regime) and the out-of-sample flat-day test run on every refit. P14 (+30 %), P06 (+23 %), P02 (+21 %), P11 (+20 %), P05 (+18 %), P08 (+17 %) and P04 (+13 %) are above the factor too. These are estimates: the factor itself varies by engine under contention (memory-bound engines suffer more), so differences under about 15 % are not attributable.
- Peak RSS rose 1.43 → 1.63 GB (+14 %).

**PG4 points (7 days, `scripts/progressive_scale.py` grid, final code, resumable, `reports/progressive/scale_r6/`).** Round 6 reads thread CPU per engine (EV6-3) and the per-event p95 as a quantile over events (the cost owner's change); round 5 read wall time and a quantile over ticks.

**Reading.**
- *Scoring.* The O-servers points improved 3.5× at 300 servers (6 941 → 1 959 µs p95) although every other number on this machine is ~1.5× slower: P03 no longer rebuilds the tree context (and re-parses every CIDR) for systems without new events. The 100 µs budget is still missed everywhere; the cost owner's section timers put the remaining ~310 µs per event on mature trees in content checks (76 µs), the per-node 'when' tables (42 µs), sequences (32 µs), combination (33 µs) and findings (28 µs) (open issue 16.14.12).
- *Learning p95* reads 1.3–2× round 5's at every point: the machine factor (~1.5×) and more at the 20 000-IP and 340-attribute points; the extra was not profiled this round.
- *CPU slope vs attributes, 0.216 → 0.293* (0.283 on the `code10` points; the per-event CPU of the 40-attribute point is 3 % lower on `code11`, that of the 340-attribute point 1 %). Per engine (`code10` points), thread CPU per event from 40 to 340 attributes (round 5's wall in brackets): P05 ×2.87 (×2.56), P02 ×1.95 (×1.87), P00 ×3.11 (×2.89), P06 ×2.40 (×1.97), **P08 ×1.81 (×1.34)**, **P03 ×1.62 (×1.24)**, **P04 ×1.43 (×1.24)**; the other engines stay within ±16 %. In µs per event at 340 attributes the growth is P05 +1 488, P04 +518, P02 +482, P00 +161, P08 +158, P03 +142. So the slope rose mostly through P04, P08 and P03 growing faster with attributes than in round 5, on top of P05 / P02 / P00, which already set round 5's slope. The tree owner's paired 5-day measurement (P04 / P05 caps) gave 0.228 → 0.221 on its own files with the others' files at the round start. EV6-7 adds ~16 ms per hourly evaluation over all 12 probes of the 340-attribute point (index dicts rebuilt on demand; `prog6/eval/memat/bench.py`), about 1 % of P05 there.
- *Memory slope vs attributes, 0.180 → 0.203 (fails by 0.003; `code10`: 0.206).* Before EV6-7 the 340-attribute point held 61.3 MB (slope 0.214): `model.attrsel` 11.9 MB against round 5's 7.5 MB, all of it the probes' interning tables (16.14.3 EV6-7). With EV6-7 `model.attrsel` is back to 7.45 MB, but `model.ptree` holds 39.3 MB against 36.9 MB on the code before EV6-8 (and 37.3 MB in round 5; `code11`: 39.25 MB, `model.attrsel` 7.48 MB): with the generalisation memo following the learned groups and windows (EV6-8), P05's level codes and so the trees at 340 attributes differ, and they hold 2.4 MB more. The 40-attribute point is unchanged (38.6–38.8 MB). The remaining excess is learned structure, not bookkeeping; open issue 16.14.12 item 8.

**Reading.**
- **Gate 15 passes in bounded mode on both packs.** Round 5's 88 / 58 stale series and 68 `pipeline_degraded` events came from the B11 / B12 prefilter (an IP with a model dropped out of the series when its score dipped), B18's members that B01 deliberately skips (now implicit idle rows, asserted equal to full mode), and two evaluator defects that EV6-4 fixed (earned-only per-IP series of demoted IPs; class keys without `feature.active`).
- **PG9 (p95 ≤ 0.5 of full) is not reachable** on these packs under §10.2's earned rule, as the B-library owner found: 30 of 37 pack A IPs earn per-IP models (B04 gain 5–130 bits per row against τ_earn = 2), so bounded mode saves only on the unearned humans. Round 5's 0.53–0.67 compared runs under different load (every engine, including the raw and derived engines bounded mode does not touch, was ~40 % cheaper in its bounded run). Raising τ_earn to 13 bits per row cuts p95 by 15 % but loses T9 (gate 8) and adds MEDIUM false alarms; not admissible. PG9 needs a design decision (16.14.12).
- **What bounded mode still costs in accuracy:** T9b on pack A (as in round 5), one more MEDIUM incident on A, and on E a refit ARI minimum of 0.461 at one refit (median 0.945). Pack A's bounded MEDIUM 10.20.4.32 of round 5 is gone (B24 health-weight hysteresis).
- **Full-mode non-regression** (default registry, against `reports/round4/runs/{A,E}_0_full.json` and round 5):
  - Pack A: detection 12/12, 8 within deadline, severities identical to rounds 4–5. Incidents ≥ LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH 18 / 7 / 2 (round 5: 19 / 6 / 2; one LOW of 10.40.4.55 on 03-13 became MEDIUM with the B24 hysteresis); reopened 9 → 8. ARI 0.780 (same). L8 medium → low (round 4's value).
  - Pack E: 3/3, severities as round 5. LOW / MEDIUM 6 / 1 (same). **Classes ARI 0.551 → 0.755 and refit ARI minimum 0.690 → 0.955**: round 4's values are back (the B-library owner's B02 role-lineage fix), with round 5's lower false-alarm count kept.
  - Gate 7: anti-conservative D⁺ maximum 0.102 (A, `marg_int`) and 0.129 (E, `marg_shape_q`), as in round 5.

**Reading the O-real example.** The 17:00 report, the approvals of 192.168.1.21 (under both the old and the renamed pages, the old one `stale`) and the finance approver are stated as in pack O, on the family tree `fam:1` that joined oa and its replica. Three things are wrong:
- 192.168.1.21's own login statement is gone on day 35 (on day 21 it was stated with confidence 0.40), so the login clause reads who-Jaccard 0.67.
- P11 put 192.168.1.21 in one group (`G18`) with the two finance clerks 192.168.2.12 / .51, whose oa logins share a family-tree login node with 10.168.7.121 and .23; the group's name is derived from its oa approval pages.
- 10.168.7.121's mail access is stated "工作日 全天（覆盖 100 %）": P09's round-6 flat-day rule (`pwindows._flat`) replaces windows whose out-of-sample coverage is below `FLAT_SHARE` by one all-day window; on 6 workdays of one address's mail sessions that is a sample-size effect (the same rule costs O60 a truth pattern, 16.14.11 item 8).

#### 16.14.11 Diagnosis of what still fails

1. **PG1 recall @14: 0.868 (target 0.90).** Precision passes now (0.960 on the observable claims; 0.877 on all claims). Recall @14 is 0.842 on seeds 3 and 4 and 0.868 on seed 2: day 14 is the Sunday after D1–D3, the new GA login window has one workday of evidence (D1, P09), and the truth already judges the new versions. The who / when / content components are 0.92 / 0.95 / 0.92. Recall @18 is 0.90 (median).

2. **PG2 calibration error 0.141 (round 5 re-scored: 0.129): the profile is under-confident, not over-confident.** Stated 0.88, held 0.94 (pooled, claims of days ≥ 7). Round 6 raised the stated confidence (0.81 → 0.88: the tree owner's p_hold changes and the 'when' checks over a trailing day) but the held rate rose with it (0.88 → 0.94: the owners' precision fixes; EV6-2 does not change pack O, whose re-scored round-5 runs hold 0.884 under both scorers). The temporal owner's decomposition (OI-4): nodes without any P04 held-out test (85 % of the claims) state 0.82–0.86 and hold 0.95–0.98. The plug-in ECE fell (0.077 → 0.060), so the reliability curve is closer; the debiased CE reads the remaining uniform gap. This is a calibration-prior question for the tree owner, not a scorer artefact: composing P09's window confidence made it worse offline (temporal owner).

3. **PG5 D4 on seed 1 (new in round 6).** One MEDIUM incident: 10.61.39.151 (a PUB portal visitor) on Saturday day 13 at 21:45 local. P03 scored its `POST /login` on node 16 with p_when = 5.8e-4 (sensitivity 2.5) and its `GET /news/{num}` on node 13 with 2.4e-4. Node 16 is a content split of the login node on `net.pkts_down` that exists only on the round-6 tree (round 5 had the `/news` LOW finding alone, so no MEDIUM incident). The portal's population uses that slot (PUB's law is normal(15:00, 4 h) to 23:00, about 9 % after 20:30), but `when_ptab`'s `max(p_hier, min(p_own, p_parent))` lets the child's own sparse non-workday counts set the floor. The temporal owner's OI-10 proposes `max(p_own, p_parent)` for a young content-split child. Not applied: it is a P03 statistics change that needs its own validation on all seeds and O-real (A4 depends on the same table), and the run snapshots hold no tree to check it offline.

4. **PG5 D1 on seeds 3–4 (unchanged, 3/5).** Seed 3 still needs 4 workdays; the temporal owner's young-regime width prior lifts its 3-workday IoU 0.62 → 0.70 (just below the clause). Seed 4 confirmed on workday 5 in round 5 and is not confirmed by day 21 in round 6: its nine new-regime logins fall in 518–530 under U[510, 531] (a ~5 % sample), and with the old regime's width as a prior the young window stays at IoU 0.65–0.68 (the checklist's login window on day 21 misses too: 0.68 against round 5's 0.71). The owner's simulation halves the failure rate of the clause (0.08 → 0.035); seeds 3–4 are the tail it leaves.

5. **PG8 arms 0.833 and the who-level clause (2/5)**: unchanged from round 5 on four seeds. EV6-5b sets portal's P08 arm `off` on seed 0 as the strategy truth expects.

6. **PG10 (OA statement day 11 / day 21) and PG11 (R-items)**: unchanged; O-real reaches R7–R10 (3–4 of 11 per seed).

7. **O-real.** Recall @35 0.35 / 0.41 / 0.34 → 0.54 / 0.66 / 0.52, precision @35 0.85 / 0.86 / 0.92 → 0.94 / 0.97 / 0.97, anomalies 4 → 7 / 6 / 5 of 10 (A3 gained on every seed, A6 on seeds 0–1, A4 on seed 0; the tree owner measured these on P00's per-row proxy resolution), the profile under-confident (stated 0.89–0.91, held 0.94–0.95). What still fails:
   - **False alarms rose** (≥ MEDIUM: 0.0012 / 0.0024 / 0.0014 → 0.0015 / 0.0025 / 0.0036). Seed 2's clean-entity incidents: about 20 MEDIUM `missing_predecessor` findings on SALES addresses 192.168.3.x, mostly `POST /docs/{num}/comment without GET /docs/{num}` on oa or oa-r2. The replica pair's load balancer sends a user's document read to one member and the comment to the other within one tick. P10's sessions are family-wide but cover only earlier batches; P03's same-batch overlay is per system batch. Before P00 resolved the proxy's clients these users were hidden behind 192.168.100.99. Open issue for the P03 / P10 owner (16.14.12).
   - **A2, A5, A7 missed** on every seed (as the owners report): A2 needs the oa login node's `net.src → username` binding (GA's login node has no binding on the family tree), A5 (report without predecessor) is not flagged, A7's `intensity` violation never becomes an incident.
   - **The example on day 35** (seed 0): the 综合部 login statement holds 10.168.7.121 and .23 only; 192.168.1.21's login statement, present on day 21 (confidence 0.40), is gone on day 35 (the temporal owner saw the family tree's statements fluctuate on days 21–35). GA bindings are stated on a mixed login node that also holds two FIN addresses, so the checklist's binding clause reads 0 / 3.
   - **Finance bindings**: O-real finance's `body.kv.username` is `redundant` with `http.ctype` on days 1–27 because the service account `svc_sync` dominates the username's probe mass (16.14.3 EV6-5); finance binds its clerks from day 31.

8. **O60 agreement (outside 0.05 in round 6; round 5 inside by cancellation).** Day-8 recall 0.500 against pack O seed 0's 0.576 (Δ 0.076), precision 0.903 against 0.938. Pattern by pattern, what O60 misses and pack O recovers is the same in both rounds: `FIN.finance.approval#0` (no confirmed statement on the first event-mode day) and `GA.oa.approvals#2` (when, content); O60's truth also has `GA.oa.documents#2` (34 rows against 33). Round 5 agreed only because O60 also recovered two patterns pack O missed, `FIN.mail#0` and `GA.oa.approvals#1`; in round 6 O60 misses both, on 'when', as pack O does:
   - `FIN.mail#0` (财务部's mail, law windows 09:15–09:33 and 13:30–14:03): the group part `p:mail:0:4@1.0|grp:dept:财务部` is stated "工作日 全天（覆盖 100 %，3 个工作日）". P09's round-6 flat-day rule (`pwindows._flat`: out-of-sample coverage below `FLAT_SHARE` → one all-day window) fires on 3 workdays of a three-address group; round 5 stated 09:15–09:25 and 13:33–14:01. The same rule states 10.168.7.121's O-real mail "全天" on 6 workdays (16.14.10).
   - `GA.oa.approvals#1` (`GET /approval/{num}`, law 09:27–11:33): stated 08:57–12:01 at coverage 0.67 (round 5: 09:27–11:30 at 0.91), IoU 0.68 against the law. Not isolated further; it matches the round-6 session-weighted fit (`_sessions`) and `_extend` on the switch from aggregated to 60-s events.
   Open issue 16.14.12 item 4.

9. **PG4 memory slope vs attributes (new failure) and CPU slope.** See 16.14.7: the 340-attribute point grew by 4.3 MB, `model.attrsel` +4.4 MB and `model.pbind` +0.6 MB, from the owners' round-6 P05 / P08 changes, not from the evaluator's EV6-5. EV6-7 removed the interning part (slope 0.214 → 0.203 on `code11`); what remains is ~2.4 MB more `model.ptree` and 0.6 MB more `model.pbind` at 340 attributes.

10. **PG9 / gate 15** (16.14.8): gate 15 passes; PG9's ≤ 0.5 is not reachable under the spec's earned rule.

11. **O-red A4, D1, D2 (new failures on the final code; 16.14.9).** A4's raw p_when at the 综合部 login node is 4.7 × 10⁻⁴, and P03's per-node calibration maps it to 0.036: the node predates D1 and its calibration ring took the drift's out-of-window logins as normal. This is a property of P03's calibration under drift (open issue 13); EV6-8 only changed which tree grew, and on `code8` the corresponding node was re-formed after the drift. D1 (2 LOW incidents) and D2 (rename not adopted by day 19) were not diagnosed further.


#### 16.14.12 Open issues (round 6 → owners)

1. **[P03 / P10, false alarms on replica families]** P03's same-batch session overlay (`conformity._score_batch`, `overlay`) is built per system batch. For the members of an engine family (O-real oa / oa-r2), the other member's events of the same tick are not seen, and P10's family-wide sessions cover only earlier batches. Proposal: score the family's member batches of a tick in one pass ordered by time, or seed each member's overlay from the other members' rows of the same tick with `ts < t`, keyed by the tree key. Target: O-real seed 2's ~20 `missing_predecessor` MEDIUM incidents on 192.168.3.x (FAR ≥ MEDIUM 0.0014 → 0.0036). The temporal owner's OI-8 (P03 scoring keyed sessions behind a SNAT address, patch in its report) belongs to the same change; it is not applied, because it changes behaviour and needs its own O-real runs.
2. **[P03, D4 seed 1]** `when_ptab` for a young content-split child (the temporal owner's OI-10): p = max(p_own, p_parent) on the day type when the split attribute is neither temporal nor a source attribute. Validate on pack O seeds 0–4 (A4 uses the same table) and O-real.
3. **[P05, O-real finance username]** `pselect.redundancy` judges redundancy on the probe's mass. A form field whose mass is dominated by one value (`svc_sync`) is a "function" of whatever marks its rows although its other values (three clerks) are not. Proposal: judge g3 also on the rows where the dependent attribute takes a non-modal value, or weight each value equally, before declaring a pair redundant. Then P08 needs no `redundant` candidates (EV6-5b).
4. **[P09, small-sample windows]** (16.14.11 item 8) The flat-day rule on out-of-sample coverage (`pwindows._flat`) states "全天, coverage 100 %" for young or sparse sources (O60 财务部 mail on 3 workdays, O-real 10.168.7.121's mail on 6 workdays); with few dates the leave-dates-out coverage is too noisy to declare "no time-of-day law". Proposal: require a minimum of independent dates / sessions before `_flat` replaces fitted windows (below it, keep the windows with their predictive coverage). Also check O60's `GA.oa.approvals#1` window widening at the aggregated → event switch (session weighting, `_extend`). Target: O60's day-8 agreement (≤ 0.05) and P09's cost (+50 % at equal load, 16.14.7).
5. **[tree, calibration prior]** Under-confidence (stated 0.88, held 0.94 on pack O; 0.89–0.91 / 0.94–0.95 on O-real): nodes with no held-out P04 test state 0.82–0.86 and hold 0.95–0.98 (the temporal owner's OI-4). The tree owner's p_hold prior is the lever; the temporal owner measured that composing P09's window confidence makes it worse.
6. **[P14 / P11 / family tree, the O-real example]** O-real seed 0: 192.168.1.21's login statement disappears between days 21 and 35; P11 groups .21 with two finance clerks (`G18`), and the family login node that holds the 综合部 addresses also holds 192.168.2.12 / .51 and carries no `net.src → username` binding (checklist bindings 0/3 on every seed). The temporal owner saw fam:1's statement count swing (52 → 23 on day 35) only after its keyed sessions (CHANGE12–14); its proposed next step is to log P15's per-tree budgets and P10's bytes on days 20–35, and to give keyed sessions their own small LRU outside the tree's session cap.
7. **[P03 / P08 / P10, O-real anomalies]** A2 (needs GA's `net.src → username` binding on the family login node), A5 (report without predecessor not flagged; six `missing_predecessor` false alarms on oa-r2 come from sessions split across the replica pair, item 1), A7 (the `intensity` violation never escalates to an incident).
8. **[P04 / P05, memory vs attributes]** (16.14.7) PG4's memory slope against attributes is 0.203 (≤ 0.2). EV6-7 brought `model.attrsel` back to round 5's 7.45 MB at 340 attributes; the excess is now `model.ptree` (39.3 MB against 37.3 MB in round 5) and `model.pbind` (1.17 against 0.57 MB: 27 binding nodes with 112 pairs against 17 with 68, i.e. more learned bindings, not bookkeeping). A per-attribute bound on what a node keeps for targets beyond the first few would be the lever; not measured.
9. **[PG4 cost]** CPU per event vs attributes 0.293 (P04 ×1.43, P08 ×1.81 and P03 ×1.62 from 40 to 340 attributes, against ×1.24 / ×1.34 / ×1.24 in round 5; P05 / P02 / P00 as before). Scoring p95 2.0 ms and learning p95 3.8 ms against 100 / 250 µs. The cost owner's remaining items: per-node 'when' tables and who closedness per tick (not equivalent; needs a lead decision and a PG1–PG10 check), P04 `HoldRecord.add_many` (exact), P02's vectorised `_distributions` (exact), a version-keyed `Hierarchies` builder for O-servers. P09 costs ~50 % more than round 5 at equal load (16.14.7).
10. **[PG9, spec]** The ≤ 0.5 p95 ratio is not reachable on packs A / E under §10.2's earned rule (30 of 37 pack A IPs earn per-IP models; paired ratios 0.94 / 0.81). A design decision is needed: an E_max relative to the system's population, or forced-only per-IP models plus the class tier for the rest, with gate 8 kept through the forced list.
11. **[B24 hysteresis, B-library]** `calib.KS_RESTORE_D = 0.035`, `RATE_RESTORE_BAND = [0.6, 1.67]` had mixed seed effects on pack A (seed 0 full: one LOW → MEDIUM, L8 medium → low; bounded: the 10.20.4.32 MEDIUM gone; seed 1: FAR identical, L8 medium → critical, round 4's value). Not confirmed on seeds 2+. Bounded pack A keeps two undiagnosed extra MEDIUMs (oa-portal 10.30.2.23 on 03-12 05:00, api-gateway 10.40.4.57 on 03-13 10:30), present in round 5 too; bounded pack E's refit ARI minimum is 0.461 at one refit.
12. **[tests, timing]** `test_b13_budget_edges::test_perf_forty_entities_generous_bound` (80 ms bound, comment "measured ~10–15 ms") fails on this machine under two concurrent runs on the round-5 code as well (76–97 ms). `test_bounded_mode.py::test_bounded_cost_flat_in_idle_known_ips` is flaky on this machine on the round-5 tree too: `signature.rule_match` iterates every known entity (a store snapshot each) and grows 3 → 52 ms per tick with 400 idle IPs. Proposal (signature owner): iterate the entities written at this tick (the engine already reads fresh values only), or the system's active set in bounded mode.
13. **[P03, calibration under drift]** (16.14.9, O-red A4) P03's per-node calibration (`ConfState.cal`, CAL_TYPES) keeps the low p of a drift's arrivals as the node's normal: on O-red the 综合部 login node existed before D1 moved the window, absorbed the new regime's out-of-window logins, and mapped a 03:05 login's p_when 4.7 × 10⁻⁴ to 0.036 (no finding). Proposal: when P09 accepts a regime change at a node (`when['drift']` / `regime_cut`), restart (or exclude the drift dates from) that node's 'when' calibration ring, as P04 restarts its structural levels with the coder. Validate on pack O seeds 0–4 (D1–D3 and A4 share the nodes) and O-red.
14. **[P08 / P09, O-red D1 and D2]** On the final code O-red fails D1 (2 LOW incidents during the drift) and D2 (10.168.7.121's binding not switched to `mike.w` by day 19); both pass on `code8`. Not diagnosed.
15. **[evaluator, O60]** The O60 agreement compares day-8 recall totals; round 5 passed it by cancellation (16.14.11 item 8). A per-pattern agreement (share of truth patterns recovered by both or neither) would not hide opposite misses.

### 16.15 Round 7: results on the final code (evaluator, 2026-10-18)

Four owners worked at the same time on top of 52e813f (round 6):
- the tree owner: P04, P05, `pnode`, `pselect`, `psketch`;
- the temporal / workflow / content / views owner: P08, P09, P14, `pwindows`, `pfd`, `prender`;
- the conformity owner: P03, `pscore`;
- the harness owner: the evaluation harness, PG9, P00–P02's input path and lib-4.

Their work is in the checkpoint commits 4a104dc, dda0658 and e65d606. The evaluator then measured the final code (16.15.1), applied the clearly-right cross-owner patches and fixed one determinism defect (16.15.3).

- 16.15.1–16.15.3 cover the method, the owners' changes and the evaluator's changes (EV7-1 – EV7-7).
- 16.15.4–16.15.10 cover the results: gates, progress with time, determinism, cost, PG9, the variants, and the user's example.
- 16.15.11–16.15.12 cover the diagnosis and the open issues.
- 16.15.13 is the harness owner's own report on the harness, bounded mode and input cost.

#### 16.15.1 What was measured

**Code state.**
- Every P-core run below used **`code7a`**: commit e65d606 (the lead's checkpoint with the four owners' work and the evaluator's EV7-1 – EV7-6). `code7a` is identical to e65d606 in `backend/` and `scripts/`.
- After the runs, the evaluator made one more change, **EV7-7**. It makes a sum in `views._group_mass` run in a fixed order. It changes only the last digit of a group-view support (16.15.6), so the scored results of `code7a` are those of the final code. The determinism pair and the PG9 runs used **`code7b`** = `code7a` + EV7-7, which is the final working tree.

**Runs.**
- Pack O: seeds 0–4, 21 days at 900 s, registry `progressive_decision`, `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`. Each run used the resumable runner (`eval/resumable.run_pack_resumable`, a checkpoint at a day end about every 15 min of wall time) and was scored by `progressive_report._score`, the report's own scorer. Driver: the evaluator's scratch `prog7/eval/drv7.py`.
- Pack O seed 0 was also run under `PYTHONHASHSEED=1` (16.15.6).
- O-red and O60: seed 0. O-real (35 days): seeds 0–2.
- Packs A and E: seed 0 with the default registry (`scripts/evaluate.py`, full mode).
- PG9, under the lead's new definition: the paired runs of `scripts/progressive_pg9.py` (pairs A and E; the 1 000-IP large point over 84 h) on `code7b`.
- PG4: round 6's grid (IPs 500 / 20 000, attributes 340, servers 20 / 100 / 300), 7 days, resumable (`pscale.run_point_resumable`), thread CPU per engine (`reports/progressive/scale_r7/`).

*An evaluation pitfall, caught and corrected.* The evaluator's code snapshots held only `backend/` and `scripts/`. `build.DATA_DIR` locates the lib-4 signature library (`data/signatures`) relative to the code, so the first runs of packs A / E and of PG9 from the snapshots ran without signatures. Their incidents differed from round 6 (pack A 12 / 7 / 1 against 18 / 7 / 2) only for that reason. The snapshots now link `data/`, and every A / E / PG9 figure below comes from the re-runs. The pack O, O-real and PG4 registries (`progressive_decision`, `progressive_only`) have no signature engine, so they were not affected.

At most two heavy processes ran at a time on the 4-core machine. The machine was markedly less loaded than in round 6: the unchanged lib-3 engines B24–B28 took 0.68× their round-6 wall time. Time comparisons with round 6 therefore carry that factor (16.15.7).

**Before and after.** "Before" means round 6's final runs and report, now in `reports/progressive/round6/` (runs, report JSON and HTML, as published). Round 6's pickles are gone, so they were not re-scored. The round-7 scorer changes two things, and they matter for the comparison:
- EV7-1: an anomaly detected on a replica of its system counts.
- EV7-5: PG2's depth is read on a paired cohort.

Both act on O-real's anomalies and PG2's depth check only. The other figures are directly comparable.

#### 16.15.6 Determinism

Pack O seed 0 was run on the final code in separate processes with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` and `PYTHONHASHSEED=1`.

- **Scores.** Identical in every pairing, with 0 differences in 17 607 leaves (`jdiff.py`, timings excluded):
  - `code7a` h0 against `code7a` h1;
  - `code7a` h0 against `code7b` h1;
  - `code7b` h0 against `code7b` h1.
- **Full result pickle, `code7a`** (deep diff, `pkldiff.py`): **8 differences**, all in the last digit (ULP).
  - They are the `support` / `n_obs` of three node-part statements in the group view of `class:grp:G69` (portal POST /comment) on days 11 and 19, for example 367.2517616673076 against 367.2517616673077.
  - Round 6 had 0 differences. The cause is EV7-7: `views._group_mass` summed the member IPs' counts while iterating a set of strings, whose order follows the hash salt.
  - That fallback is taken when the group key is not among the node's grp-level heavy hitters.
- **Full result pickle, `code7b`** (the final tree, with EV7-7): **0 differences** between `PYTHONHASHSEED` 0 and 1 (`prog7/eval/det7b_h{0,1}`). Every event, incident, snapshot model, statement and value is equal.
  - Against `code7a`'s h0 run, `code7b` differs in exactly the same 8 last-digit values and nothing else.
  - The published `code7a` runs are therefore the final code's results to the last printed digit.
- **Subprocess hash-seed tests.** The owners' tests pass (`test_p04_p05_stream_equivalence.py`, `test_registry_hash_order.py`, `test_round5_hash_order_views.py`, `test_round5_eval_order.py`), and so does the evaluator's new `test_round7_hash_order_views.py` (6 hash seeds).

- On pack O the user's example is learned in full on seed 0. The login statement states the three addresses, the 08:31–08:51 window, the 1–2 KB / 1–2.8 KB size, the `username=` grammar and its closed set, the three bindings, and the login → home flow.
- The approval and report statements carry the right who, window and content. The department view states 综合部's use of oa and mail, and its three closed negative statements on crm, finance and portal; the finance negative names .23's denied attempt.
- After the D3 rename the old approval route is shown as `stale` beside the adopted new one.
- On O-real (day 35) the system view is the family `fam:1`. The approval and report statements are right. The 综合部 login part lists two addresses, while 192.168.1.21 sits in a group named after its approval actions with finance's .2.12 / .2.51. The user view of that group therefore mixes two departments. P11 has no department configuration on O-real, so there is no department view.

#### 16.15.11 Diagnosis of what still fails

1. **PG1 recall @14: 0.868, unchanged; the target is 0.9.**
   - At the median seed 33 of 38 truth patterns are recovered on day 14, and the target needs 35. The misses per seed on day 14 (`per_pattern`):

     | Pattern | Seeds missed | Failing components | Cause |
     |---|---|---|---|
     | GA.oa.report#1 | 5/5 | who, when, content | reaches 20 observations on Friday of day 12, which is exactly the eligibility threshold. N_CONF = 20, the daily lifecycle, the weekend and the next-day reference put its statement at day 15 (tree owner's diagnosis; lowering N_CONF trades away precision) |
     | DEV.oa.login#0 | 5/5 | content | the truth's username set has 60 values, which no closed-set statement holds (OI-e) |
     | GA.mail#0 | 4/5 | who / when | GA's mail parts are split across sibling /16 nodes (OI-d) |
     | FIN.finance.approval#1 | 4/5 | content | the approval opinion field is not closed by day 14 (n ≈ 20; OI-e) |
     | FIN.mail#0 | 3/5 | who, when | — |

   - Seed 4 also misses GA.oa.report#0 on day 14: it is confirmed on day 16, against day 13 in round 6.
   - Recall is unchanged elsewhere on days 3–18. On day 21 seed 0 gains 0.872 → 0.923 (the tree owner's release fix, PUB.portal.visit#3).
   - Seed 1 loses GA.oa.approvals#1@1 on days 19–21. It is a workflow edge at dependency 0.806, just above P10's acceptance cut, and it flaps (P10 open issue).
   - Seed 4 loses GA.oa.approvals#0@1's time clause on days 20–21.
2. **PG2 calibration: error 0.141 → 0.066, stated 0.94 against held 0.94.** The target is ≤ 0.05.
   - Round 6's under-confidence is gone on every pack O seed (stated − held: −0.06 → −0.003 at the median).
   - What remains is the bin structure, not the mean. On seed 0, node claims are under-confident (0.94 stated, 0.97 held) and group parts over-confident (0.94 stated, 0.91 held). On seed 2 the opposite holds (nodes 0.96 / 0.94, parts 0.95 / 0.98).
   - O-real stays at 0.089–0.115 and O-red at 0.244 (stated 0.79 against held 0.94: under-confident, as in round 6).
3. **PG2 "confidence of unchanged patterns non-decreasing (paired)": 5/5 → 2/5. This is a gate-semantics issue, not a regression of the profile.**
   - The failing steps have median paired changes of −0.0037 (seed 1, days 5 → 7, 12 patterns), −0.0006 (seed 3, days 10 → 21, 26 patterns) and −0.0036 (seed 4, days 10 → 21, 26 patterns).
   - These happen at a stated confidence of 0.95–0.98. Round 6 stated 0.88–0.90 there, and the rule asks for a median change ≥ −1e-9.
   - Once confidence saturates near the held rate, sampling noise of a few thousandths decides the check. The gate is unchanged; proposal for the lead in 16.15.12.
4. **PG1 "GA + FIN bindings 6/6 at day 14": 5/5 → 4/5. On seed 2 only 3 of 6 bindings are counted.**
   - On days 12–15 GA's login statements are `evolving`, with confidence 0.016–0.019, while D1 moves the login window. P14 now composes the time clause as `pwindows.window_hold` (CHANGE7), the posterior probability that the window holds.
   - The bindings are intact on those days (lower bound 0.99), but the check counts bindings in confirmed statements only.
   - Round 6, the temporal owner's own runs (mine4) and the conformity owner's (c5) show the same thing on seed 2; the tree owner's n19, without CHANGE7, does not.
   - A statement whose window is in transition is rightly not confirmed. The bindings it carries are not in transition, though, and P14 has no way to state them separately (open issue).
5. **PG4: CPU / event slope against attributes 0.293 → 0.260 (61 % of the growth is P05 and P02). The scoring and learning p95 are still above their budgets** (16.15.7).
6. **PG5.**
   - D1 3/5: seeds 3–4 have too few samples at three workdays (OI7-4, unchanged).
   - D4 4/5 → 5/5: FIX2.
