#### 16.20.11 Diagnosis of every regression

The scorer's new lists (item 0) name every failed claim's statement and failed constraint, and every FAR incident's constraint kinds, so most items below are traced from the final runs themselves. Of the failed constraints on pack O seeds 1–4 (days ≥ 7), **97 are `when.workday`** window coverages and 11 `when.nonworkday`, 81 payload clauses (`body.*`: grammar / closed sets / bands), and 24 claims had no held-out event of their context.

1. **Pack O precision @21 on seeds 0 and 4; the precision @14 median.** Seed 0's day 21 fails four claims, every one on `when.workday` coverage: `p:mail:0:1@2.0` (stated 0.996; coverage 0.960, held 0.923), `p:portal:0:4@1.0` (0.884 / 0.800), and two configured-department parts at OA nodes, `p:oa:0:3@2.0|grp:dept:财务部` (0.844 / 0.511) and `p:oa:0:6@1.0|grp:dept:财务部` (0.889 / 0.827). Each owner's own run keeps round 11's 0.968 (`B3s0`, `v8m`, `b10`); the bisection points place it as an interaction: `bis_VB` (views + bounds) 0.968 with the portal and 财务部 `oa:0:3` failures, `bis_LV` (learn + views) 0.952 with `mail:0:1` added, the merged tree 0.935 with `oa:0:6|财务部` added. The windows themselves are P09's (`time_window.py`, unchanged since round 11); what changes is which statement and part is judged and with which held-out draw (one stream per claim key). The coverage P09 states for a broad law exceeds the held-out coverage by up to ~0.1 after cross-validation — the bounds owner's open item 5 (pack O seeds 0 / 1 / 3: stated 0.966 / 0.981 / 0.973 against held 0.961 / 0.969 / 0.962 for claims ≥ 0.9, most failures P09 window coverages) — and the configured-department parts at OA nodes (views, T11-4 / round 12's `_dept_colleagues`) state the node's window for a subset of its sources. Seed 4 (0.960 / 0.966 → 0.940 / 0.949) is the learning file's: `bis_L` (`code11` + `pattern_tree.py` + EV12-1) reproduces it exactly (0.940 / 0.949, and precision @7 0.933, CE 0.068) while `bis_V` (views alone) has 0.980 / 0.966; the failures it adds are portal windows (`p:portal:0:5@1.0` `when.workday` 0.933 / 0.882 on day 14, `p:portal:0:3@1.0` `when.nonworkday` 0.914 / 0.780 on day 21) and `p:oa:0:5@1.0` (`when.workday` 0.969 / 0.920 on day 14; on the merged tree day 14 fails `p:oa:0:18@1.0|grp:G9`'s `body.len` band, 0.80 / 0.73, in its place) — born_tl changes which portal / OA nodes are confirmed with which rows by day 14. Owners: bounds (P09 window coverage), views (department parts' windows); not a clear defect, no fix before the final runs.
2. **Pack O CE 0.060 → 0.066, ECE @14 on seeds 1 and 4.** CE rises on seeds 0, 1, 2, 3 (0.041 → 0.047, 0.060 → 0.063, 0.078 → 0.080, 0.060 → 0.074); the learning owner's own runs show the same rise (`B3s0` 0.050, `B3s3` 0.077): born_tl adds summaries (and so held-out-tested constraints, mostly P06 `net.*` bands the scorer does not judge) to young nodes, whose internal held-out failures lower their stated confidence into the 0.6–0.8 bins while the scorer's held-out passes — under-confidence (seed 3: stated 0.953 → 0.947, held 0.950 → 0.956). This is item 1b, which the lead's decision 2 keeps unchanged this round. ECE @14 on seeds 1 / 4 adds the day-13–14 username claims at `p:oa:0:14` / `p:oa:0:3|grp:dept:综合部` (`body.kv.username.grammar` / `.closed` held 0.68–0.96: D2's rename on day 12 meets a prefix who that now covers .121 — views, inherent to the rename).
3. **Pack O FAR ≥ LOW median 0.0013 → 0.0014.** Seed 0 0.0009 → 0.0014: three single-tick `alarm` incidents on crm sources (192.168.3.36 day 3, .31 day 4, .29 day 6; no `pattern_violation` constraint — B-library alarms on empty evening slots) that `b10` alone has too (0.0013; the bounds owner's open item "crm empty-slot single-tick LOWs"), plus one from the learning file (`bis_LV` 0.0011). Seed 4 0.0007 → 0.0009: two LOW `alarm` incidents on 192.168.9.9 (oa day 8, portal day 15). ≥ MEDIUM is at or below round 11 on every seed (max 0.0007; seed 1's D4 incident is gone: b10's exposure-normalised when scoring). Owner: bounds.
4. **Pack O precision @7 on seeds 2 and 4.** The OA approve node states `body.kv.opinion` closed on day 7 (seed 2 `p:oa:0:9@1.0`, seed 4 `p:oa:0:10@1.0`: closed set held 0.73 / 0.90 against nominal 0.94 / 0.95; seed 2 also fails `p:oa:0:10@1.0`'s window and `p:portal:0:3@1.0`'s night window on day 7) because born_tl keeps the opinion summary from the node's birth; 退回 (rare) then fails the closed set on held-out draws. The same mechanism finds GA.oa.approvals#2 on days 5–10 of seeds 0 and 3. Owner: learning (P07's set closure on a week of a rare value; the trade is net positive on precision @7: median 0.938 → 0.968).
5. **O-real seed 1 recall @35 0.734 → 0.709.** The rows lost are the moved finance clerk's OA rows after R3's move, FIN.oa.login#1@1 (lost on days 29–35, also 22–23) and FIN.oa.login#0@1 and FIN.oa.documents#0@1 (lost on days 34–35; round 12 finds login#0@1 on days 29–33 only, documents#0@1 on 9 of its 24 days against 19); in exchange GA.oa.approvals#2@1 (days 20–30), GA.oa.report#1 (days 23–28) and FIN.oa.documents#2@1 (days 19 and 22–28) are found, and SBR.oa.documents#1 on days 31–35. `bis_V` (`code11` + the views owner's files alone) reproduces the loss exactly (recall @35 0.709, precision @14 0.953, CE 0.101; FIN.oa.login#0@1 found on one day, #1@1 on days 24–28 only), so the owner is views. Not traced further; the candidate is the round-12 `_dept_colleagues` rule (a learned group adds members to a configured department only when at least half of its configured members belong to that department), which decides whether 财务部's configured parts at the OA nodes name the moved clerk's new address. The rule fixes T11-4's defect on seeds 0 and 2 (the 综合部 who clause back), so it is kept; the trade on seed 1 is open (16.20.12 item 6).
6. **O-real seed 0 recall @10, precision @14, CE, R4; seed 2 CE and FAR ≥ LOW.** Seed 0's day-9–11 losses (DEV.oa.login#1, GA.oa.login#1) and the CE rise (0.075 → 0.097: under-confidence of the family login node's parts) are the views owner's v7 measurement (CE 0.101, recall @10 0.767): `who_groups._peel` changes the early groups, so the family tree splits differently (`fam:1` node 13 is gone) — the same change that moves R4's 09:40 login from node 13 (p_when 0.00098, LOW) to a node where it scores p_when 0.0102 (the views owner's `r4g` bisection: v8m + `code11`'s `who_groups.py` restores R4). R4's round-11 pass was a when-window knife edge; the credential axis is data-limited (rose2 one event by day 11, `pending` in `pfd.classify`). Seed 2's FAR ≥ LOW 0.0021 is round 11's tree-side level (crm-03 alarms; the learning owner's diagnosis); R11 still fails on the portal growth after the scanner (0.143), with lead decision 3's measure.
7. **O-red recall @21 0.886 → 0.864 and FAR ≥ LOW 0.0007 → 0.0009.** GA.oa.approvals#2@1 is lost on days 20–21: the renamed approve node `p:oa:0:26`, born on day 16, was ranked by P05 on day 19; B3's birth list ended by age on day 18, the bounded cap dropped its `body.len` summary and the band restarted, so the node stated a one-day band on day 20 (the learning owner's trace). B6 (birth list until P05 ranks the node, ≤ 7 days) recovers the row but turns the day-12 OA requests of three sources (192.168.8.104 / .107 / .111) at `p:oa:0:0` into `novel` + `new_action` + `below_range` MEDIUM incidents (EV12-2), so it was not landed. Owner: learning.
8. **O60 precision @7 0.933 (target 0.967).** The views owner's own snapshot reaches 0.967; on the merged tree a young 综合部 mail part (`p:mail:0:4@1.0|grp:dept:综合部`, confidence 0.645, `when.workday` coverage 0.50 held 0.29) and the portal's night window (`p:portal:0:6@1.0`, `when.nonworkday` 0.917 / 0.812) fail. Owners: views (department part of a young node) and bounds (P09 small-n night window).

#### 16.20.12 Open issues (round 12 → owners)

1. *The round-12 bar.* Met: pack O D4 5/5 and FAR ≥ MEDIUM ≤ 0.0007 on every seed, O-red precision @21 (0.955), O-real seed 0 recall @35 (0.759), O-real seed 2's 综合部 who clause, checklist (8/10), D2 and bindings @14 (5/6), the four reverse clauses of pack O seed 0's login, pack O seed 3's GA.oa.approvals#2 on days 6–10, and every keep item but one. Not met: pack O FAR ≥ LOW median (0.0014 against 0.0011), precision @14 median (0.950 against 0.967; pooled 0.965), precision @21 median (0.973 against 0.975), CE (0.066 against 0.059), O-real seed 2 FAR ≥ LOW (0.0021) and R11, O60 precision @7 (0.933), and the keep item O-real seed 1 recall @35 (0.709 against 0.722).
2. **P09 window coverage over-statement (bounds; the main precision limiter).** Most failed claims fail on `when.workday` coverage; P09's stated coverage exceeds the held-out coverage on broad laws after cross-validation, and the KS young cut fires on broad laws (pack O seed 1 visit#3 days 18–19). Proposal for the bounds owner: state the coverage of a cross-validated window as the CV estimate's lower bound (not the in-sample coverage), and measure on pack O seeds 0–4 that precision @14 / @21 and CE improve without recall loss.
3. **Configured-department parts' windows (views).** Parts `grp:dept:财务部` at OA nodes and `grp:dept:综合部` at young nodes state the node's window for a subset of its sources (held 0.29–0.83 against 0.50–0.89). Proposal: a department part states its own sources' window (P09 on the part's rows) or none when its rows are fewer than P09's `min_points`; test on pack O seed 0 day 21 (`oa:0:3` / `oa:0:6`).
4. **Item 1b, under-confidence from unjudged facets (learning, lead decision).** born_tl raises CE on 4 of 5 seeds through internal held-out failures of P06 `net.*` bands that the scorer does not judge. The lead's decision 2 kept item 1b unchanged in round 12; the measurement for the decision: CE 0.060 → 0.066 with stated 0.953 → 0.947 and held 0.950 → 0.948 (median), i.e. the stated confidence now sits on the held-out rate on average but not per bin.
5. **O-red's GA.oa.approvals#2@1 (learning).** B3 loses it on days 20–21 (birth list ends by age before P05 ranks the renamed node); B6 keeps the birth list until P05 ranks the node but turns three sources' day-12 OA requests into MEDIUM `novel` incidents. Root cause to trace in the learning owner's next round: why a longer birth list changes `p:oa:0:0`'s day-12 novelty for three sources (`pg6.far.incidents` names them).
6. **O-real seed 1's moved-clerk OA rows (views)** — 16.20.11 item 5. `bis_V` reproduces it. Proposal for the views owner: a readdressed address (P11's `readdressed` map, which R3's move fills on every O-real seed) joins its old address's configured department in every part the old address had, independently of the learned-group bar; test on O-real seed 1 day 35 (FIN.oa.login#0 / #1@1) and keep seeds 0 and 2's 综合部 who clause.
7. **R4 on O-real seed 0 (views + bounds).** The 09:40 credential test scores p_when 0.0102 at the node where the early groups now place it; the round-11 pass was a knife edge. The credential axis needs more than one event of rose2 by day 11.
8. **crm single-tick LOW alarms on empty evening slots (bounds)** — pack O seed 0's FAR ≥ LOW 0.0014; seed 4's two LOW alarms on 192.168.9.9.
9. **T11-5 / T11-6 (learning; lead decision d).** They stay reverted: with born_tl they make crm-03's node judge a group-level `net.src@3 → http.ua` binding before the group's members were seen (O-real seed 2 FAR 0.0041 / 0.0028). Root cause in P08 / `lib/pfd` (judging a group-level binding whose members were not all observed); proposal: `fit_pair` leaves a group-level source unjudged until every member of the group has `n_bind` observations at the node.
10. PG11 R11's growth measure is unchanged (lead decision 3: the dumps of the post-scanner portal splits did not finish).
11. O-real seed 1's A5 (rounds 8–12) and the O-real FAR ≥ LOW on seeds 1 / 2 (0.0021) remain from earlier rounds.

## Appendix A. Review changes (adversarial review, 2026-09-29)

The first draft was reviewed sentence by sentence against the user requirement (§3) and
against the state of the art it cites. Each row lists what was wrong or missing, the change,
and where it now lives. Nothing here has been implemented or measured; every number added by
the review is either a default with its reason (§7.1) or an estimate, like the rest of the
document.

| # | Finding (what was wrong or missing) | Change | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| RC1 | **Requirement gap: servers.** S1 forbids traversing all users *and servers*. Every system had a fixed ≈ 20–30 MB tree and fixed hourly/6-hourly fits, so memory and CPU grew linearly with the number of servers; a new server started from nothing. | System families (shared tree, `net.dst` as an ordinary split attribute: "一类服务器 → 某一台服务器"), activity-proportional tiers incl. XS, checkpoint-out of idle trees, dirty-node periodic work, cold start by family inheritance; PG4 server curves; pack O-servers; R9, R13. | PPC-10, §6.20, §6.19, §7, §11.6, §12 PG4 |
| RC2 | **Statistical error: evidence inflated by mass.** ω = H(r + m) − H(r) let one aggregated row count ≈ ln m units and a thinned HT row (weight up to ~1 000) ≈ 7 units; split statistics and Dirichlet predictives used mass counts, so HT weights made nodes look far more certain than the learner's observations justify. | Mass and evidence separated everywhere: ω ≤ 1 per observed row (harmonic within a run), evidence-scaled predictives, split statistics in evidence units, sensor sample rate scales mass only. | PPC-9, §5.2.3, §6.5.3–6.5.4, §6.13 |
| RC3 | **Statistical error: split significance.** The summed prequential saving (a ratio of two Bayes mixtures) is not a test martingale under a composite null, double-counts dependent targets, and "C_eval counts every evaluation" was an unjustified charge; the Bernstein check was a fixed-n bound applied repeatedly. | Rule (V): per-target universal-inference e-values (pooled ML code length vs prequential split code), averaged over targets (valid under any dependence), Ville's inequality ⇒ anytime-valid; multiplicity charged per candidate (log2 i ⇒ ≤ 2^−τ0 · H(C_ever)); MDL sum kept as gain (G); time-uniform Bernstein for (S); learning restarts after R_learn; system-level false-split rate stated; exceptions use the same test with a conservative leave-x-out construction; revision and alternates use an explicit τ0 margin. | PPC-11, §6.5.5, §6.6, §6.7, P04 tests (b)–(b″) |
| RC4 | **Statistical error: decay vs bounds ("越久越准" violated).** All confidences used H_m-decayed evidence, which plateaus at rate × 10 d: the finance approval node's U could never fall below ≈ 0.016, so its HIGH-candidate severity (U ≤ 0.01) and the P03 test fixture (n_eff = 200) were unreachable; single-IP exceptions (n_eff,x ≥ 20) and node invariants (n_eff ≥ 50) were unreachable for once-a-day sources. | Confidence channel: H_l evidence reset to the H_m state on an accepted change, capped while evolving; shape stays on H_m. Confirmation, closedness, bindings, bounds, invariants, exceptions and statement support use it; the remaining plateau is stated with examples. | §6.9.4, §5.5.3, §6.8.1, §7.1 |
| RC5 | **Statistical error: range bound.** The 30-day observed range was paired with the H_m n_eff; the rank bound 2/(n+1) needs the number of observations the extremes were taken from. | Daily ring of (min, max, n_obs) over the confidence segment; n_rng; render threshold 30 (was 50, unreachable for small nodes by day 14). | §6.10 |
| RC6 | **Multiple testing on emissions.** A busy IP was tested per event against fixed thresholds; FAR per entity-day grew with the IP's event count. | Emission thresholds on p_day (Šidák over the IP's scored events at the (node, type) that day); expected chance emissions per clean IP-day bounded. | §6.16.3, P03 test (h) |
| RC7 | **Who violations conflated DHCP and intruders.** A never-seen IP had grp = ∅ and was flagged `outsider_group` ⇒ HIGH candidate on every re-addressing; A8 had no rule distinguishing credential reuse from re-addressing. | `outsider_group` only for grouped IPs; `unknown_ip`; binding concurrency test (`concurrent_use` vs `readdress_candidate`); provisional P11 join; heavy-set definition; severity rows updated; A8 made explicit. | §6.12, §6.15, §6.16.2–6.16.3, §11.4 |
| RC8 | **Poisoning gap.** A single foreign source that persisted for 5 days could be accepted into a who-closed node (single-IP persistence rule), and an attacker not yet in an incident learned at full weight. | Who-set changes need a group already present, a readdress candidate, a label, or (σ < 2) ≥ 2 sources of one group; outlier damping for p ≤ 1e-4 events; P02/P10/P11 learn from t − D with trust; new anomaly A9 (low-and-slow) with a non-adoption check. | §6.9.2–6.9.3, §4.2, §11.4, PG6 |
| RC9 | **Hidden per-IP enumeration / unbounded state.** P01 built a window event for every active IP each grain (96 store reads each); P03's intensity counter beyond its cap sampled new pairs with weight 10 (false alarms possible); B04 shadow LRU of 100 000 IPs (≈ 60 MB per system); P13 composed a portrait for every IP every 2 h; batches of all events were retained 2 h (≈ GBs at 5 000 events/s) and not counted in §7; retired summaries and group views were uncapped; P05 swept all 512 attributes hourly. | W_max with priority sampling; intensity SpaceSaving scored on guaranteed counts plus a separate `pat.rate` batch; B04 shadow only for heavy candidates with shrinkage; P13 IP portraits earned-only; batches compacted to learned rows, retained D + 1 ticks, M_batch/M_tick in §7, R_tick cap; retired summaries ≤ N_max/2; G_max group views; P05 rotating slice; all LRU caps allocated by P15 from the sources seen. | §6.2.3, §6.16.4, §10.2, §6.17.1, §5.2.3, §5.6, §6.8.2, §6.15, §6.4, §7.2 |
| RC10 | **Infeasible budget.** `cpu_ms_per_tick` = 80 ms (the gate-14 latency figure) while lib-3 already needs ≈ 909 ms at 35 entities and the P-core ≈ 1–2 s per 900-s tick: the ladder would have been engaged permanently, and ladder step 5 touched B-engines even in full mode. | Budgets as CPU share and memory, P-core separate from lib-3; ladder step 5 only in bounded mode; step 7 priority scoring under overload; e_rate default 10/s. | §6.19, §7.1, §13.2 |
| RC11 | **Metrics still hard-coded.** Sampling strata, P05 context seeds and code-type hints were fixed lists. | Stratum from the tree's own root split; seeds are bootstrap only; type hints are configuration with a data test. | §6.2.2, §6.4, §5.3 |
| RC12 | **Schema changes looked like behaviour changes.** A missing split attribute sent every event to `other`. | Absence is a value (`⊥`); `attribute_gone` detection; splits on gone attributes collapse. | §5.2.2, §5.5.1, §6.3, §6.6, R10 |
| RC13 | **Missing real-world cases.** No treatment of SNAT reverse proxies, NAT/VDI, shared terminals, service accounts, IPv6 privacy addresses, holidays vs weekends, month-end jobs, scanners, sensor sampling, late logs, new servers, binary bodies. | Who resolution (XFF, trusted proxies, `snat_suspect`), `shared:<ip>`, `sess.key`, set bindings, `/64`, `ctx.dayclass`/`dom`/`mend`, normal-day counting, dormant patterns, outlier damping, sample-rate mass; a situation table with signals, responses and residual limits; pack O-real (R1–R13) and PG11. | §5.1.4, §5.4, §6.2.3, §6.8.1, §6.12, §6.21, §11.4, PG11 |
| RC14 | **Grammar example inconsistent with the algorithm.** `[a-z]{1,10}` was presented as learned from jack/rose/mike, which anti-unification cannot produce; PG10 required "at most `[a-z]{1,10}`" although D2 introduces `mike.w`. | Length bounds are observed with coverage; operator-pinned business bounds via B23; example shows `[a-z]{4}`; prefix factoring specified; PG10 split into day 11 and day 21 checks with `[a-z.]{1,10}`. | §6.11, §6.17.2, §3 S8, PG10 |
| RC15 | **Evaluation could not prove its claims.** PG10 at day 14 conflicted with D1 (day 12) and with the range render threshold; weekly patterns could not be confirmed in 14 d (3 dates needed); A9 was missing though recall was "over 10 anomalies"; nothing measured "precision grows with time", false splits, servers, or real-world conditions; the red-team variant was undefined. | PG1 opportunity rule with ≥ 3 dates; PG2 weekly ≤ 21 d, confidence-growth and false-split checks; PG4 server dimension; PG6 A9; PG10 re-timed; PG11; packs O-real, O-red (with 20 independent attributes), O-servers defined. | §11.6, §12 |
| RC16 | **Workflow poisoning and id reuse.** P10 counted every current event (including an attacker's) into the DFG; SpaceSaving eviction could reuse an action id. | DFG counts from learned trusted rows of t − D via `prev_act` in `pat.assign`; ids never reused; sessions keyed by (ip, sess.key). | §6.14 |
| RC17 | **Strategy selection maths.** Hedge ran on a gain/cost ratio (unbounded losses); the who-level code was not a complete code for unseen items. | Utility in one currency (bits − λ_c · µs), clipped for Hedge; ratio only for knapsack packing; who-level two-part code with escapes specified; B-engine applicability arm. | §6.18.2 |
| RC18 | **Bindings.** The empirical-Bayes prior reused x's own data; no representation for shared terminals or service accounts; the example numbers were not reproducible. | Leave-one-out prior (numbers recomputed with scipy: 5 pure logins ⇒ LB ≈ 0.88), set bindings both directions, `sess.key` bindings behind NAT. | §6.12, P08 tests |
| RC19 | **Value policy vs requirement.** Production default HMAC would never show `username=jack`, the requirement's own example; secrets were caught by key name only. | Default clear for non-secret values (legal out of scope), secrets shape-only by key glob and value randomness (reusing `lib/template._looks_random`), long values shape-only; lead confirmation kept as an open item. | §5.1.3 |
| RC20 | **"自动学到综合部".** Names were said to come from config only, which reads as manual upkeep; the requirement expects the department to be recognised. | Stated plainly: membership is learned, a name needs a source; IPAM / DHCP-scope / asset / directory import script. | §0 item 6, §2, §6.15 |
| RC21 | **No end-to-end trace.** An implementer could not see how the example emerges (which splits, when groups arrive, when each fitter can speak). | Worked trace of the OA example, day by day, with the portal contrast. | §6.22 |
| RC22 | Small fixes: `p_ref` NaN before the first snapshot; ancestor-sampling uniform keyed by `seeded_uniform`; `rate_Hs` defined; P02 statistics from t − D; lag list in §9.1; family pseudo-system store keys; new events (`attribute_gone`, `pattern_revived`, `family_changed`); references added (Ville, universal inference, e-value combination, time-uniform bounds, priority sampling). | as listed | §5.6, §6.5.1, §6.8.3, §9.1, §15 |

**Open items for the lead** (added or changed by the review, beyond the architect's list):

1. The value-policy default (RC19) supersedes the decisions.md privacy line for the PPC.
2. Contract additions grow: `compact_batch` on the store (RC9), the `pat.rate` batch, the
   `fam:<id>` pseudo-system key for shared trees (RC1), and `model.sysfam`.
3. The confidence plateau (H_l = 30 d, RC4) is a product trade-off: longer H_l means more
   confidence for unchanging behaviour and slower forgetting of changes no detector flags.
4. Pack O-real extends pack O to 35 days for R8; eval wall time grows accordingly.
